nodes.label: Practice runs
nodes.rationale: A throwaway card and throwaway pull request take a machine through its steps before that machine ships, and the note records what those runs change.

nodes.label: World's four contributions
nodes.rationale: The world lends only type, palette, density, and one signature move; it never supplies layout, navigation model, or controls.

nodes.label: Empty States
nodes.rationale: Empty states are onboarding opportunities: they should explain what will appear, why it matters, and how to get started rather than showing blank space.

nodes.label: Product Color
nodes.rationale: Product defaults to Restrained color; accent is reserved for primary actions, current selection, and state indicators, not decoration.

nodes.label: Product Components
nodes.rationale: Every interactive component needs default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, and error states; consistent affordances across the surface are a virtue.

nodes.label: Product Layout
nodes.rationale: Responsive behavior is structural (collapse sidebar, responsive table, breakpoint-driven columns), not fluid typography.

nodes.label: Product Motion
nodes.rationale: Users are in flow; motion conveys state, not decoration, so 150–250 ms transitions and no orchestrated page-load sequences.

nodes.label: Product Constraints
nodes.rationale: Modals are usually laziness; exhaust inline and progressive alternatives first.

nodes.label: Product Permissions
nodes.rationale: Product can afford system fonts, standard navigation patterns, and density that brand surfaces can't; consistency over surprise is a virtue.

nodes.label: Product Slop Test
nodes.rationale: Product UI's failure mode isn't flatness, it's strangeness without purpose; the bar is earned familiarity and the tool should disappear into the task.

nodes.label: Product Typography
nodes.rationale: Product UIs don't need display/body pairing; a fixed rem scale and tighter ratio (1.125–1.2) suit consistent-DPI task viewing better than fluid clamp sizing.

nodes.label: Operate Mode
nodes.rationale: The visitor completes a task; scanability, consistency, native expectations and the real usage scene outrank expression, with brand living in precise details.

nodes.label: Read Mode
nodes.rationale: The visitor understands something; structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.

nodes.label: Directions
nodes.rationale: Expression may never obscure the task, state, or familiar affordance.

nodes.label: app/favicon.ico
nodes.rationale: Next's icon decoder rejected the first attempt outright with 'The PNG is not in RGBA format!', which failed the whole page rather than the icon alone, so the source was converted to an RGBA PNG inside the ICO container.

nodes.label: perf-validated.mjs
nodes.rationale: Streaming TTFB excludes Linear completion, so full-response measurements are retained too.

nodes.label: PR #372
nodes.rationale: Ready list, Start and Back built; CI green with real slow-read and performance proof recorded.

nodes.label: impeccable comp-diff
nodes.rationale: Produces side-by-side, heatmap, one paired crop per region, and report.json; the side-by-side is the view the build thread never has on its own, and a region scored missing or contradicted is a fix whatever the page looks like from memory.

nodes.label: impeccable detect
nodes.rationale: On hookless web builds it is the only slop gate; a native platform skips it entirely because it reads HTML and CSS and has no verdict on native code.

nodes.label: impeccable-documenter agent
nodes.rationale: The documenter cannot ask and writes nothing over an existing DESIGN.md without the user's refresh/overwrite/merge choice.

nodes.label: impeccable-finish-reviewer agent
nodes.rationale: Spawned fresh with no forked conversation history, because a reviewer that inherits the transcript inherits the builder's framing, optimism, and abstractions; it has no browser, so screenshots not passed are checks it cannot run.

nodes.label: Capture validity rules
nodes.rationale: A capture is evidence only when it is valid: settle or disable entrance motion first, capture full-page from the document top, and open every file once to confirm it shows what its name claims — a malformed capture sent onward costs the whole round.

nodes.label: Disposition: recapture
nodes.rationale: The evidence failed, not the build; a review conducted on invalid evidence binds nothing and a verdict pass may never follow it.

nodes.label: Disposition: ship
nodes.rationale: Nothing is owed; report the verdict at its scope and continue to the documenter. A refused ship is an unfinished build.

nodes.label: The first viewport is a thesis, not a header
nodes.norm_label: the first viewport is a thesis, not a header
nodes.rationale: The memory test: if someone left after one viewport, what would they describe an hour later? If the honest answer is a mood, the concept has not committed yet.

nodes.label: Phase 3: hero (first viewport)
nodes.rationale: This is where the run's ambition is won or lost, and a retry here costs minutes where a rebuild verdict at the finish costs the run; plates are placed before any text so plate regions can be read as match first.

nodes.label: Step 7: Inspect and finish
nodes.rationale: Two inspection rounds is the ceiling and fixes batch between them; after the second round polishing is over and whatever remains ships through the handoffs, where a fresh context does the finding better and cheaper.

nodes.label: Phase 6: responsive
nodes.rationale: The gate refuses a first viewport that only held at the comp's exact width, so sizes are proportional to the viewport rather than px floors and nothing the comp's first viewport shows is pushed below it.

nodes.label: PRODUCT.md

nodes.label: Comments

nodes.label: Subagents

nodes.label: Writing the reply
nodes.rationale: A cleanup pass after drafting does not remove these patterns, so the reply is written clean as drafted.

nodes.label: Poteto Mode
nodes.rationale: Bundled skills live at ../<name>/SKILL.md relative to this file, so this file's absolute path must go in every poteto-agent prompt.

nodes.label: Contrarian Framing
nodes.rationale: If two reviewers will surface principle X, find the principle Y that complicates or contradicts X.

nodes.label: Divergent Lens
nodes.rationale: The obvious learning from a session is rarely the most useful one; second-order effects and paths not taken are what other reviewers miss.

nodes.label: Scope Findings to Skills Actually Used
nodes.norm_label: scope findings to skills actually used
nodes.rationale: Speculative routings to skills the parent never opened do not count; only invoked skills or missed-trigger candidates are valid targets.

nodes.label: Durable Principle Extraction
nodes.rationale: State the rule, not the label; surface only principles that survive code drift.

nodes.label: Already-Covered Criterion
nodes.rationale: If existing guidance is buried, weak, or easy to skip past, reframe the proposal as a wording or placement improvement rather than a duplicate addition.

nodes.label: Convergence Criterion
nodes.rationale: Findings echoed by two or more reviewers carry higher confidence; singletons must clear a higher bar.

nodes.label: Decision-Changing Criterion
nodes.rationale: A future agent must do something different because of the edit, not just read more text.

nodes.label: Durability Criterion
nodes.rationale: A finding must still be true once paths, SHAs, tool versions, and code shapes have changed.

nodes.label: Existing-Skill-First Criterion
nodes.rationale: Propose a new skill only when no existing skill is a real home, the pattern recurs, and the topic deserves its own skill.

nodes.label: Accepted / Rejected / Backlog Output
nodes.rationale: The user approves accepted rows one by one; the parent applies them after approval.

nodes.label: Skill-Was-Used Criterion
nodes.rationale: Accept only findings that route to a skill, tool, or MCP the parent invoked; otherwise reject as skill-not-used.

nodes.label: Specificity Criterion
nodes.rationale: Broad enough to apply across tasks, precise enough that a future agent recognizes when to use it.

nodes.label: Structural-Mechanism Check
nodes.rationale: Route to backlog when a lint rule, script, metadata flag, or runtime check already enforces the rule or could enforce it cheaply; skill prose is for things mechanisms cannot enforce.

nodes.label: Agent Self-Sufficiency
nodes.rationale: Flag every moment the user manually supplied context the agent could have fetched itself via an MCP tool or sibling skill.

nodes.label: 0001 The board shows only the machine's work
nodes.norm_label: 0001 the board shows only the machine's work
nodes.rationale: Agents opened by hand (Command Code, Codex) leave no run record the dashboard could read, and all card work is meant to go through the machine.

nodes.norm_label: 0002 every card belongs to a project that finishes
nodes.rationale: Each piece of Julia and each machine change gets its own project so nothing sits in a never-ending project like machine-setup or Maintenance; a 7-day window and Linear milestones were rejected.

nodes.label: 0003 Compare any model in any role
nodes.norm_label: 0003 compare any model in any role
nodes.rationale: Decision support compares models per role, not per card or per single builder model; a card counts only for roles that actually ran on it.

nodes.label: 0004 A card's trace is deleted when its retro is complete
nodes.norm_label: 0004 a card's trace is deleted when its retro is complete
nodes.rationale: The old factory's traces reached 10-15 GB per round and stopped the factory when the drive filled; the retro is the last thing that reads the trace, and the committed scorecard keeps the numbers.

nodes.norm_label: 0005 mint & iris look; the phone board is a folding list of stages

nodes.label: Comment Sicko
nodes.rationale: A read-only reviewer with a short keep list, so a surprise in your own code gets no pass.

nodes.label: Build the change and clean the diff
nodes.norm_label: build the change and clean the diff
nodes.rationale: Build playbooks share one discipline: say what you observed and let the playbook demand the evidence; cleanup is not optional polish because padded diffs read as unfinished and hide the next bug.

nodes.label: /benchmark-checklist
nodes.rationale: A before-and-after number is the easiest evidence to get wrong by accident, so seven questions each demand evidence from a run.

nodes.label: /no-comments
nodes.rationale: Comments need a pass from someone who did not write them, because an author defends its comments the way you would defend yours.

nodes.label: Bug fix playbook
nodes.rationale: Supplies the step the prompt leaves out: reproduce before fixing.

nodes.label: Feature playbook
nodes.rationale: Supplies the step the prompt leaves out: name the data shape before implementing.

nodes.label: Hillclimb playbook
nodes.rationale: Loops one hypothesis at a time against a frozen measurement harness, keeping wins and reverting everything else.

nodes.label: Opening a PR playbook
nodes.rationale: Runs cleanup on the diff before each commit and on the prose, because five narrow PRs beat one fat one.

nodes.label: Perf issue playbook
nodes.rationale: Supplies the step the prompt leaves out: profile before optimizing, and vet the baseline and every number after it.

nodes.label: Refactoring playbook
nodes.rationale: Supplies the step the prompt leaves out: pin behavior before restructuring.

nodes.label: Runtime forensics playbook
nodes.rationale: Instruments the running process to get the cause before any fix; it returns a diagnosis, not a fix.

nodes.label: Trace forensics playbook

nodes.label: Confidence Tiers

nodes.label: Direct Evidence Tier
nodes.rationale: An explicit, textual citation answers the question: something an author actually wrote that says why, not code behavior.

nodes.label: Inferred Evidence Tier
nodes.rationale: A reasonable reading of the context that nothing explicitly supports; it is the analyst's interpretation, not a fact from the record.

nodes.label: Handling Missing Evidence
nodes.rationale: An honest 'we don't know' is valuable; filling a gap with a confident guess harms the user because they will act on it.

nodes.label: Phrasing Guide
nodes.rationale: Confidence words imply Direct or Supported evidence and need an adjacent citation; hedges signal interpretation rather than report.

nodes.label: Speculative Evidence Tier
nodes.rationale: A plausible hypothesis on thin evidence where other explanations fit equally well; worth presenting but must be marked as a guess.

nodes.label: Supported Evidence Tier
nodes.rationale: Multiple pieces of indirect evidence converge on one conclusion even though no single source states it explicitly.

nodes.label: Unknown Evidence Tier
nodes.rationale: A valid and important outcome: you looked and could not find out, and must document specifically what was searched.

nodes.label: Investigator Epistemic Discipline
nodes.rationale: Mechanics are not motivation; no intent from code behavior or style, preserve uncertainty, and gather rather than conclude.

nodes.label: Investigator Output Format
nodes.rationale: Structured findings (searched, direct, indirect, contradictions, gaps, leads) so the synthesizer can read them directly.

nodes.label: Synthesizer Epistemics Framework
nodes.rationale: Every claim must sit in one tier, Direct/Supported claims need citations, and gaps must be documented rather than filled with plausible-sounding guesses.

nodes.label: Synthesizer Instructions
nodes.rationale: Merge overlaps, surface contradictions, calibrate each claim, spot-check citations, and leave open questions open rather than overreaching.

nodes.label: Synthesizer Investigator Findings Input
nodes.rationale: Investigators gathered raw evidence, not conclusions; the synthesizer weighs the evidence itself.

nodes.label: Synthesizer Output Format
nodes.rationale: Fixed structure (Question, Code, What We Found, Inferred, Competing Hypotheses, What We Don't Know, Sources Consulted, Confidence Summary) so the reader knows what is known, inferred, and missing.

nodes.label: Synthesizer Quality Check
nodes.rationale: The value of the output is its honesty, not its authority; a confident-sounding answer on weak evidence is the exact failure the skill exists to prevent.

nodes.rationale: DESIGN.md asks for diamond or leaf glyphs in the centre of section dividers, but the shipped dividers are plain hairlines.

nodes.label: Cook mode (full screen)
nodes.rationale: Step text scales from 24 px on phone to 48 px on desktop so it is legible at arm's length while cooking; swipe, arrow keys, space, i and Esc are wired for hands-busy use.

nodes.label: machine/merge/gate.mjs
nodes.rationale: The machine does not judge the change and does not trust a local artifact; it reads the pull request's own comments. A verdict that judged an older commit refuses the merge, because the branch moved after the review. This rule lives only here.

nodes.label: machine/merge/land.mjs
nodes.rationale: Uses --match-head-commit so the forge itself refuses when the branch moved after the verdict. Branch deletion is left to sweep because --delete-branch deletes the local branch too, which fails on any checkout holding it, and a merge that succeeded would read as a fault.

nodes.label: machine/merge/retro.mjs
nodes.rationale: A retro that does not end with 'RETRO: written <path>' is a failed retro, not a passed one; the reflection heading is checked, not trusted.

nodes.label: machine/merge/sweep.mjs
nodes.rationale: Removes only what this card left behind: never touches main, never touches a branch whose commits main does not hold, refuses anything under docs/scorecards/ so the cost rows stay, and never removes its own run folder.

nodes.label: machine/merge/workflow.mjs
nodes.rationale: Every step saves the run record before handing on, so a crash leaves finished steps in record.json and a rerun continues from there instead of merging twice.

nodes.label: Shipping agent verdict
nodes.rationale: The machine lands only when the newest Shipping agent comment for this card and pull request is PASS or PASS+NOTES and the commit it judged is the commit the branch points at now. Every Shipping agent determination for the card and pull request counts as one review round.

nodes.label: docs/scorecards/<CARD>.landing.json
nodes.rationale: The scorecard is generated from Mastra's records and would overwrite anything appended to it, so the landing facts go beside it in a separate file.

nodes.label: clear-before-upload.cfg
nodes.rationale: Models one regression of the real code; the run fails if the checker ever stops catching it, because a property no configuration can break proves nothing.

nodes.label: fresh-id-on-every-write.cfg
nodes.rationale: Models one regression of the real code; the run fails if the checker ever stops catching it, because a property no configuration can break proves nothing.

nodes.label: Standard platform components
nodes.rationale: Every control must be a standard one the visitor already knows how to use, never a costume of the world's own interface.

nodes.label: State colours
nodes.rationale: State colours sit on top of the world's palette only where they carry meaning.

nodes.label: Frame
nodes.rationale: The world's palette, type, and signature move commit fully in the frame (masthead, navigation rail, ground, title and section openers, code/table/callout setting) so the page could belong to no other product.

nodes.label: Navigation and Wayfinding
nodes.rationale: Navigation and controls stay the standard ones for the platform; the world never replaces navigation with something a reader has to learn.

nodes.label: Reading Column
nodes.rationale: The reading column stays calm — a reading face, real contrast, a real measure, nothing performing behind the text — because the world must never supply the reading order or make the reader learn new navigation.

nodes.label: Self-check
nodes.rationale: A render must let a reader tell where they are and where to go next and read the body comfortably; if it reads as an artifact of the world before a document, the world has reached the column and must be pulled back to the frame.

nodes.label: Signature Move
nodes.rationale: One system used where it earns its place, never a frame repeated around every element.

nodes.label: The World
nodes.rationale: Candidates from the world's own publishing traditions transfer best; a tool, instrument, or fictional interface returns as a costume on a reading page, so only type, palette, density, and one signature move are taken.

nodes.label: Comps
nodes.rationale: A variant that adds world material, texture, or ornament goes further in the wrong direction; on a working screen, more world is a costume.

nodes.label: Comps
nodes.rationale: The comp is the document as the reader meets it: a frame the world owns around a calm reading column at a real measure.

nodes.label: Directions
nodes.rationale: The reader's question leads, and comprehension and wayfinding stay intact at every step; documentation must still read as documentation.

nodes.label: Comps Two and Three
nodes.rationale: Each goes further than the first, never cleaner: a bolder use of the same world, a larger or stranger focal move, or a composition the category would not attempt.

nodes.label: Material Coverage
nodes.rationale: A world reduced to an accent on a neutral template is the category default with a sticker on it; the world's material should be the ground and major surfaces.

nodes.label: Object-as-Page (One Object, One View)
nodes.rationale: The object keeps its real form: a book opens to two pages on one gutter, never a third panel, and more content goes on the object's own surfaces or the next spread below.

nodes.label: World as Carrier, Not Picture
nodes.rationale: The world may be the carrier of the page, never a picture of it; a viewport painted whole with no working parts is a picture of the world, not its website.

nodes.label: Onboarding Analytics
nodes.rationale: Track completion and drop-off points to verify onboarding quality.

nodes.label: Contextual Tooltips
nodes.rationale: Teach features at the point of use, when users need them, rather than upfront.

nodes.label: Interactive Tutorials
nodes.rationale: Hands-on practice in a sandbox is preferred when concepts are complex or the stakes are high.

nodes.label: LocalStorage Seen-State Tracking
nodes.rationale: Show onboarding once: track completion and respect dismissals so returning users are not shown initial onboarding again.

nodes.label: Onboarding
nodes.rationale: Onboarding's job is not to teach the product; its job is to get people to the moment that proves the product is worth their time.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Teaching one thing at a time avoids overwhelming users with information upfront.

nodes.label: Skip / Optional Onboarding
nodes.rationale: Experienced users should be able to bypass onboarding; blocking access to the product patronizes them.

nodes.label: Time to Value
nodes.rationale: Teach the 20% that delivers 80% of value; front-load the most important concepts and save advanced features for contextual discovery.

nodes.label: --auto flag
nodes.rationale: --auto produces horizontal band scaffolding, not element identification; it is optional and does not replace authoring a map.

nodes.label: baked-composite flag
nodes.rationale: A raster region whose note names a frame and the view it opens onto is flagged so the plan and asset review shows it to the user first.

nodes.label: COMPARE sheets
nodes.rationale: Open the comparison sheets first to inspect affected crops together, then open individual crops where more detail is needed.

nodes.label: Containment
nodes.rationale: Parent and children keep separate IDs and crops; containment never transfers approval.

nodes.label: Painted material
nodes.rationale: If a region is painted material (a figure, a photograph, a metal or paper surface), classify it plate, image or texture now rather than leaving the catch to the user.

nodes.label: regions.json
nodes.rationale: Each region needs a stable id, kind, note, and exactly one of pixelBox, normalized box, or grid, using the original comp's dimensions.

nodes.label: Region Map
nodes.rationale: A region map names what is actually visible in the approved comp before asset production; it is not a page build or an asset approval. Comp crops are reference evidence only, never production assets, and zero errors does not certify crop accuracy.

nodes.label: Orchestrate
nodes.rationale: You run the program, never the code: decide which agent does each piece of work, then check what each one produces. One task driven to a predicate is an Autonomous run; one ambitious run needing a bespoke workflow is figure-it-out; work one agent could finish inside the session budget is not a program.

nodes.label: Shipping
nodes.rationale: You own what lands: verify each PR independently, land only the verified run from the root, then keep your hands off the stack. Only a verdict from an agent that did not write the code counts, because an author checks what it meant to build.

nodes.label: Bugbot triage
nodes.rationale: The goal is not to ignore Bugbot by default; it is to stop treating every comment as a required code change. When in doubt, ask — skipping a noisy code-quality comment is cheap, skipping a real data or security bug is not.

nodes.label: Session pickup
nodes.rationale: You own the resume point: read the prior trail, don't redo it. The prior trail is authoritative input; resist the bias to re-derive it.

nodes.label: Worktree and simulator cleanup
nodes.rationale: This is the one playbook that deletes user state with no code review to catch a slip, so the gates above are the review.

nodes.label: Attack the Premise
nodes.rationale: Each failed fix is evidence against the belief it assumed. A third fix on the same premise spends effort where the evidence already says the cause is not.

nodes.label: Build the Lever
nodes.rationale: A codemod, generator, or script does the work the same way every time and reruns for free; the tool is one artifact a reviewer can read and rerun. Hand-done changes can only be re-verified by redoing them.

nodes.label: Databricks Notebooks
nodes.rationale: Notebooks are not queryable via the SQL MCP, so suspected rationale living in a notebook must be reported as a gap rather than a null result.

nodes.label: Event Usage Trajectory Pattern
nodes.rationale: A step function from zero to steady volume within a day or two of a merge is strong circumstantial evidence the PR launched the feature; decay to zero suggests deprecation or deletion.

nodes.label: Experiment / Feature-Flag Lookup Pattern
nodes.rationale: Experiment and feature-flag schemas are company-specific, so tables must be probed with SHOW TABLES before names are assumed.

nodes.label: Guard-Rail Threshold Origin Pattern
nodes.rationale: A p99 of the relevant properties_<name> column in the 14 days before the PR that matches the target's threshold constant suggests the number was chosen from data.

nodes.label: Query-History Evidence Pattern
nodes.rationale: Filtering system.query.history by statement_text with a tight start_time window surfaces the expensive queries that likely motivated a migration, backfill, or perf rewrite.

nodes.label: Typed dbt Models (stg_*)
nodes.rationale: Typed dbt models are deduplicated, typed, and liquid-clustered, whereas the raw analytics_track_event table has duplicates and untyped properties_json; drop to raw only when no dbt model exists or events fall inside the dbt refresh lag.

nodes.label: Time-Bounded Queries
nodes.rationale: These tables are huge and unconstrained scans time out, so every query filters on _timestamp or start_time with a window bracketing the ship date (~30 days either side).

nodes.label: Databricks Analytics & System Tables
nodes.rationale: Databricks is the product/data view (what users did, which experiments ran, how feature usage evolved, where a threshold constant came from), complementing Datadog's infra/runtime view.

nodes.label: Backup
nodes.rationale: Refreshed overnight on days something changed; only changed files are touched.

nodes.label: Cook mode
nodes.rationale: Screen is kept awake and steps are advanced by tap zones or voice so the cook can work hands-busy at the stove.

nodes.label: Dish
nodes.rationale: A recipe appears at most once per menu.

nodes.label: Menu
nodes.rationale: Past menus move to a Past list by themselves.

nodes.label: Prep list
nodes.rationale: Ordered back from serving time; regenerating keeps Todd's manual changes.

nodes.label: Real Julia
nodes.rationale: Only accepted changes reach it.

nodes.label: Recipe
nodes.rationale: Stored as written; everything else (total time, conversions, scaling, badges, nutrition) is derived on display.

nodes.label: Yield
nodes.rationale: Scaling changes the number; nutrition is per one of the word.

nodes.label: Guide: Set up pstack
nodes.rationale: Setup is one command plus a short conversation; of everything in the guide the verification skill pays off the most.

nodes.label: /create-formal-verification-skill skill
nodes.rationale: Tests check the cases someone thought to write; a formal verification skill checks one key property in every case within a stated scope.

nodes.label: /create-verification-skill skill
nodes.rationale: An agent that can check its own work keeps going until the check passes; an agent that can't hands every result back to you to check by hand.

nodes.label: /setup-pstack skill
nodes.rationale: You only override what you care about: a role with no line in the model rule keeps the skill's default, so the config stays small.

nodes.label: /how
nodes.rationale: Grounds a design in the code it touches before any sketch is produced.

nodes.label: /why
nodes.rationale: Run when a design moves ownership or layers, to recover the reasoning behind the current shape.

nodes.label: Design before you write code
nodes.rationale: One attempt at a hard design locks in the first shape the model thought of, so design is settled through prototypes and competing attempts before implementation.

nodes.label: /architect
nodes.rationale: Settles types and boundaries before implementation; treats repeated workarounds or any/forced casts as proof the design is wrong and restarts instead of patching.

nodes.label: /arena
nodes.rationale: Runs N parallel attempts at the same brief, cross-judges them, picks a base and grafts the best parts so the first design is never taken.

nodes.label: /interrogate
nodes.rationale: A finding survives only when rerunning its command shows a failure that breaks the intent, so adversaries are wasted on an abstract plan with no code behind it.

nodes.label: Multi-phase plan playbook
nodes.rationale: The plan is the deliverable: one section per PR ending in proof, and a passing test suite alone does not count as that proof.

nodes.label: Prototype playbook
nodes.rationale: Prototypes are planning with code: they answer the agent's own open questions by running something instead of asking, and leave room for an option nobody thought of.

nodes.label: /setup-pstack
nodes.rationale: Supplies the configured model panel that /arena draws its candidates from.

nodes.label: /technical-writing
nodes.rationale: Named when the doc itself matters, so a tutorial stays a tutorial instead of drifting into reference and explanation at once.

nodes.label: Design illustration (three robots drafting competing bridge models)
nodes.norm_label: design illustration (three robots drafting competing bridge models)

nodes.label: Keep-List Exceptions
nodes.rationale: The only leash on deletion: legal/license headers, non-obvious behavior forced by an external dependency/platform/vendor/protocol, prettier-ignore, lint suppressions whose rule is faulty or style-only, doc comments defining a public API contract, and issue/RFC links explaining a constraint code cannot express.

nodes.label: MUST KILL Flag
nodes.rationale: Flags the exact guilty symbol for rename, extract, type, or rearchitecture so the behavior becomes obvious without prose; the agent identifies refactor targets but never writes application code.

nodes.label: REVIEW Keep
nodes.rationale: A comment claiming a rule of an external dependency, platform, vendor, or protocol survives only when the rule cannot be checked; it is then quoted word for word under REVIEW with the rule it claims.

nodes.label: Blast Radius Skill
nodes.rationale: Listing the callers is not the job — the agent can grep those in a second; the job is the breakage grep won't show you. A blast-radius writeup that sounds right is worthless because it reads as convincing whether or not it is true, so the one or two facts the change's safety depends on must be proven by running real code rather than asserted.

nodes.label: Explainer Prompt Template
nodes.rationale: Explorers each investigated a different angle and their findings overlap and may contradict, so the explainer must reconcile them and resolve contradictions by checking the code itself rather than concatenating the slices.

nodes.label: Explorer Prompt Template
nodes.rationale: Other explorers investigate different slices of the same subsystem in parallel, so each explorer is told not to cover everything and to go deep on its assigned angle instead.

nodes.label: How Skill
nodes.rationale: Explain at the level of a senior engineer onboarding onto a subsystem — enough to build a working mental model, not so much that it reads like annotated source code. When in doubt, take the simple path.

nodes.label: Comment Sicko
nodes.rationale: Comments are treated as meat by default: when it is unclear whether a keep clause applies, the comment dies, because a long justification without a proven keep-list exception is a confession and should be fixed by reshaping the code (rename, extract, type, rearchitecture) rather than by prose.

nodes.label: /loop
nodes.rationale: Cursor's built-in wake mechanism, not a pstack skill; it re-checks the finish condition on events or a heartbeat.

nodes.label: Cursor Project
nodes.rationale: Gives one coordinator agent a persistent thread; subagents run in the cloud by default so work continues when the laptop is closed.

nodes.label: Finish Condition
nodes.rationale: A checkable predicate that can pass or fail; a duration is not a finish condition because it gives the agent nothing to check.

nodes.label: Overnight Contract
nodes.rationale: A good handoff has the goal, the finish condition, permissions, and an escape hatch; it turns the goal into checks every iteration can run and pre-answers permissions so the agent does not block.

nodes.label: Pitfall: Duration Is Not a Finish Condition
nodes.norm_label: pitfall: duration is not a finish condition
nodes.rationale: 'work on this for 4 hours' gives the agent nothing to check, and you'll wake up to four hours of motion instead of a result.

nodes.label: Scheduled/Event-driven Automation
nodes.rationale: Removes the step of starting every loop manually.

nodes.label: Software Maintenance Stages
nodes.rationale: Triage, reproduce, fix, verify; every stage can stop the line and every stage hands over evidence so bad work does not reach the next stage where it costs more to undo.

nodes.label: Verification Swarm
nodes.rationale: A swarm of fresh verifiers checks the owner's code-ready head; a later rebase or minor fix gets one fresh verifier, and only new behavior or a large new diff calls the full swarm again.

nodes.label: Isolated Worktree
nodes.rationale: Keeps the run from colliding with anything else you have open.

nodes.label: Evidence Over a Green Build
nodes.rationale: A build only proves the code compiles; real evidence is the command, flow, stored value, or profile output.

nodes.label: Verification Before Looping
nodes.rationale: A loop that cannot verify its own work only makes unchecked work faster, so the verification skill must work first.

nodes.label: Worktree Isolation for Parallel Agents
nodes.rationale: Parallel agents in one worktree overwrite each other and nobody can tell which agent changed what, so each attempt needs its own worktree or a cloud agent.

nodes.label: Autopilot-full Playbook
nodes.rationale: Runs a queue of independent PRs to merged; no owner merges on its own verdict, and only a clean verdict on the patch that merges authorizes the merge.

nodes.label: Autopilot-stack Playbook
nodes.rationale: Autopilot-full without the merge, chosen when you want your own eyes on the work before anything merges.

nodes.label: Orchestrate Playbook
nodes.rationale: For a program that outlives any single agent; the coordinator decides which agent does each piece, checks what each produces, and never writes code itself.

nodes.label: Pause Safely Playbook
nodes.rationale: Finishes or backs out of the current step, commits a work-in-progress checkpoint, and writes a resume note so a fresh chat can pick the work up.

nodes.label: Authoring or Modifying a Skill Playbook
nodes.norm_label: authoring or modifying a skill playbook

nodes.label: impeccable detect
nodes.rationale: The bundled detector runs over local files: no network, no npx; it reads HTML/CSS, so it is skipped for native projects.

nodes.label: $impeccable live
nodes.rationale: live, generate and the bundled detect are web-only; the browser overlay and HTML rule engine do not apply to native app code.

nodes.label: impeccable signals
nodes.rationale: Signals are reasoned over, not scored: there is no score to obey.

nodes.label: Cream paper background #FDFCF7
nodes.rationale: Never pure white; used as the paper background for every page, card, input and cook-mode surface.

nodes.label: Forest green #2D4F36
nodes.rationale: The intended vintage token for headings and primary text; also the PWA theme colour.

nodes.label: Terracotta token #D67D61
nodes.rationale: The intended vintage accent token; components mostly bypass it with #C35231.

nodes.label: Custom server
nodes.rationale: The unit has to start the app with a host and port from the env file and the app must answer before systemd considers the start finished; next start can do the first but not the second, so server.js uses the documented programmatic entry point.

nodes.label: Provider names per account
nodes.rationale: One account can answer to more than one provider name; naming only one of the names drops the models filed under the other before pricing runs, which is how 72 of 74 CommandCode models disappeared for a day.

nodes.label: Turbopack root
nodes.rationale: The first build discovered the ancestor configuration and bundled Julia instrumentation, so turbopack.root is set to the dashboard folder.

nodes.label: Factory (build and review pipeline)
nodes.rationale: Factory's tests and independent review now stand between a builder and a merge, answering the old concern that agents worked around Firebase's offline quirks.

nodes.label: Firebase Spark plan
nodes.rationale: Chosen because its plan page names no inactivity pause; the only stop is exceeding the free quota, and household use sits far below the Spark limits.

nodes.label: Cloud Firestore
nodes.rationale: Keeps a copy of the data on each device, allows offline read/write and syncs on reconnect; one service replaces Supabase and PowerSync.

nodes.label: PowerSync (sync service)
nodes.rationale: Free account paused after a week idle in late September 2026; to be deleted once Firestore is live.

nodes.label: Supabase (Postgres database)
nodes.rationale: Project julia-next paused after seven idle days; to be deleted once Firestore is live.

nodes.label: Second free Firebase test project
nodes.rationale: Tests run against real Firestore with no Java emulator and no fakes, answering the old concern that Java emulators overloaded the runner.

nodes.label: Vercel, Sentry and Axiom
nodes.rationale: Unchanged from ADR 0005.

nodes.label: ADR 0010: Firestore on Firebase's free Spark plan for Julia's data
nodes.norm_label: adr 0010: firestore on firebase's free spark plan for julia's data

nodes.label: Voice and copy
nodes.rationale: The app speaks like a mid-century family cookbook — "scholarly yet domestic", evoking leafing through a cherished family-heirloom cookbook of the Julia Child era; utility text is typewritten uppercase mono and loading states read like a librarian.

nodes.label: Voice add
nodes.rationale: Julia reads the household's Google Keep list through a second Google account that exists only for that.

nodes.label: Julia Child
nodes.rationale: Julia is named for Julia Child, who inspired Todd to cook; 'established 1961' refers to that.

nodes.label: Tina
nodes.rationale: Cooks and shops occasionally, so screens must work for an occasional user without any learning.

nodes.label: Vintage cookbook feel
nodes.rationale: Fixed brand commitment: a cookbook that has been used and loved, never new or sterile; no food photos.

nodes.label: Julia
nodes.rationale: A household cookbook that goes beyond storing recipes: it invents recipes, plans meals and handles shopping so Todd can go from an idea to a cooked meal in one place.

nodes.label: End-to-End Relevance
nodes.rationale: A helper that takes 1% of a request can make the request at most 1% faster, however fast the helper gets.

nodes.label: Count Errors
nodes.rationale: Rejections are often fast, and timeouts and retries are slow.

nodes.label: Name the Limiter
nodes.rationale: If a change did not move the number, the limiter explains why, so find it before you call the change useless. Profile in a run you do not report.

nodes.label: Reproducibility
nodes.rationale: Run each side at least 5 times, alternating, so warmup, lazy initialization, caches, and drift favor neither. A gap smaller than the run-to-run variation is no measurable difference.

nodes.label: Tuning Parity
nodes.rationale: If one side runs on defaults, you compared configurations, not implementations.

nodes.label: Did the Work Happen
nodes.rationale: Lazy code and timeouts produce numbers for work that never happened.

nodes.label: Benchmark Checklist Skill
nodes.rationale: Vet a perf measurement before you report or act on it; answer each question with evidence from a run, not a guess about the code.

nodes.label: recipe-detail-verbatim
nodes.rationale: Text fidelity is the whole feature; toHaveText collapses whitespace, so the saved spec compares textContent strings instead, because a trimmed comparison passes while the page is wrong.

nodes.label: recipe-double-save
nodes.rationale: The recipe id is minted once, when the form mounts. That is what makes a double Save one recipe; re-minting it per submit would store two.

nodes.label: Investigator Assigned Source
nodes.rationale: One investigator per evidence category; each goes deep on its assigned source only to avoid duplicated work and confused scope.

nodes.label: Investigation Loop
nodes.rationale: Cast a wide net first, read items fully, follow links only within the assigned source, quote verbatim, and record what was searched as well as what was found.

nodes.label: Source Playbooks Index
nodes.rationale: Maps each evidence category to a concrete playbook so investigators can adapt a common MCP to the same category.

nodes.label: Incident Postmortem Playbook
nodes.rationale: Added when target code looks defensive (null checks, retry, timeout, rate limit, feature flag, egress guard, OOM handler) so the investigator runs incident-flavored queries.

nodes.label: Datadog Incidents
nodes.rationale: An incident whose timeline includes the defensive check being added is near-direct evidence for why the code exists.

nodes.label: Linear Project Docs
nodes.rationale: Project-level documents are where specs and rationale are most often captured.

nodes.label: Notion Docs
nodes.rationale: Notion is where 'why' often lives in long-form before it becomes code; a significant feature usually has a doc.

nodes.label: Incident-Related Git Commits
nodes.rationale: Commit messages like 'fix for incident', 'add defensive check', or 'revert' followed by 're-apply with...' are strong signals of incident-driven code.

nodes.label: Parent / Sub-Issue Tree
nodes.rationale: Sub-issues are tactical; parents often carry the 'why'.

nodes.label: Linear Labels
nodes.rationale: Labels hint at the category of motivation (customer-request, incident-followup, compliance).

nodes.label: Linear Tickets
nodes.rationale: Linear is where the product/business context often lives: the 'we're doing this because customer X asked' or 'this is for the Q3 compliance initiative' layer.

nodes.label: analyze_issue_with_seer
nodes.rationale: Seer's AI root-cause analyses are a hypothesis generator; the actual events and stack traces are the primary evidence.

nodes.label: Custom Mode
nodes.rationale: A Custom Mode stays in context every turn until the user exits the mode and stays out of casual turns, whereas attaching the skill with Enter fades as the chat moves on.

nodes.label: Playbook
nodes.rationale: Playbooks are step lists inside /poteto-mode, not skills, so they have no slash command.

nodes.label: Principle
nodes.rationale: Principles are one-rule skills that /poteto-mode reads and cites in its replies; the user rarely invokes one and steers with the names instead.

nodes.label: /poteto-mode
nodes.rationale: A good prompt states the goal and how to tell it's done and does not list skills, because a hand-written sequence tends to drop or reorder steps the playbook would keep.

nodes.label: Poteto Help Skill
nodes.rationale: For a help question, don't start the work: the user asked how, and a pstack run spends real tokens, so let them send the prompt. A message that asks for work is not a help question and should be run under poteto-mode instead.

nodes.label: Ornament characters (❧ ☙ • · → ← ✕)
nodes.rationale: The masthead line is exactly ❧ THE JULIA COOKBOOK ☙, with the reversed hedera mirroring the left glyph; the ❧ also opens every helper sentence on forms.

nodes.label: Codebase Improvements
nodes.rationale: Agents copy what exists and take the shortest path, so make the easy thing the right thing: better architecture, stronger types and invariants, clear boundaries.

nodes.label: /correct (pstack command)
nodes.rationale: In pstack, /correct is the inverse pyramid as a working procedure.

nodes.label: Human Review
nodes.rationale: Hardest to scale; at the rate agents land code it is impossible to thoroughly review every PR, so spend the effort on designing an environment where agents do the right thing by default.

nodes.label: Inverse Pyramid of Agent Corrections
nodes.rationale: Most effort should go to the top of the pyramid (codebase improvements) and least to the bottom (human review), because code-level fixes are deterministic, token efficient, and eliminate a class of problem permanently.

nodes.label: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
nodes.rationale: Its rule is 'the instruction is the symptom' — encode the lesson in structure rather than in prose.

nodes.label: Prose (comments, rules, AGENTS.md, skills)
nodes.rationale: Anything that cannot be enforced and requires agent judgment; use it minimally.

nodes.label: Static Analysis
nodes.rationale: Lint rules, tests, CI and verification (e.g. TLA+) are very token efficient ways to catch issues ahead of time.

nodes.label: Clipper
nodes.rationale: Sends the page as the browser sees it, plus its address, into Import; on phones the same job is done by sharing a link to Julia.

nodes.label: Cookbook
nodes.rationale: Book recipes can't be shared.

nodes.label: Import
nodes.rationale: Machine-readable recipe first, then the on-device reader, then a model only for what the reader can't handle; neither ever rewrites the text.

nodes.label: Keep screen
nodes.rationale: The only way an import enters the library.

nodes.label: Library
nodes.rationale: There is no other grouping: no folders, tags, or categories.

nodes.label: Recent strip
nodes.rationale: Shown only when the search box is empty.

nodes.label: Shared page
nodes.rationale: The only thing in Julia the outside world can see; Stop sharing removes it, and book recipes never appear on one in full.

nodes.label: Library (product capability)
nodes.rationale: One alphabetical list with search and an Under 30 minutes switch; no folders, tags or categories.

nodes.label: Shared page (product capability)
nodes.rationale: The only public surface, for read and print; book recipes never appear on one in full.

nodes.label: Craft Floor
nodes.rationale: A live session shipped five invented kickers and the documenter wrote their style into DESIGN.md; that is how one violation becomes the house style. A craft-floor refusal must never be canonized into the system.

nodes.label: Direction Contract (THESIS, OWN-WORLD, STORY, FIRST VIEWPORT, FORM)
nodes.norm_label: direction contract (thesis, own-world, story, first viewport, form)
nodes.rationale: The OWN-WORLD block names the world; the build shows how it landed. Where they diverge, the build wins and the prose may note the divergence.

nodes.label: Not-Canonized Line
nodes.rationale: Elements the floor bans are recorded as defects the build carries, never as design-system rules for future surfaces to inherit.

nodes.label: Token Schema
nodes.rationale: A value earns its place by the build and by legibility, never by making a finding disappear.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md
nodes.rationale: Records the project's design system after the build is done, derived from durable, reused rules in the build.

nodes.label: Impeccable Documenter
nodes.rationale: Ground truth is the shipped artifact: every token and rule must be evidenced by the built code, never by what was planned. Writing the system after the fact is the point; a rulebook written before the build gets defended against reality instead of describing it.

nodes.label: reference/document.md
nodes.rationale: It is the operating spec for DESIGN.md's format, token schema, sidecar, and section order, and must be followed exactly.

nodes.label: Two ways to do one task
nodes.norm_label: two ways to do one task

nodes.label: Caller's Usage First
nodes.rationale: The usage is the spec. The two must agree, so reconcile the sketch to the usage, not the reverse.

nodes.label: Rationale Template
nodes.rationale: The prose that ships alongside the type sketch. One page. Sentence-case headings, no boilerplate.

nodes.label: Alternatives Considered Section
nodes.rationale: Required. Judge each alternative on interface depth, not implementation simplicity alone.

nodes.label: Problem Section
nodes.rationale: Name the constraints the design must honor so the reader sees the same constraints you saw.

nodes.label: Shape Section
nodes.rationale: The type sketch is derived from the usage; when they diverge, reconcile the sketch to the usage, not the reverse.

nodes.label: Synthesis Decision Section
nodes.rationale: Filled in by arena. Records which candidate became the base and why, what was adapted from each of the others, and what was rejected and why.

nodes.label: Tradeoffs Accepted Section
nodes.rationale: Name anything a future reader might mistake for an oversight, including things that look like premature optimization or premature simplification.

nodes.label: Usage (Caller's View) Section
nodes.rationale: Write this first, before the type sketch. The caller's experience is the spec. The types serve it.

nodes.label: Phase A: Frame
nodes.rationale: Every candidate gets the same prompt, so the prompt is the contract.

nodes.label: Phase B: Fan Out
nodes.rationale: Spawn all N subagents in one message in the background, each with its own output path.

nodes.label: Phase C: Cross-Judge
nodes.rationale: The judge is never from the parent's family, so the verdict is not self-confirming.

nodes.label: Phase D: Pick a Base
nodes.rationale: Pick the base a future maintainer can extend most easily without breaking invariants. When two feel tied, prefer the cleaner boundary or smaller API.

nodes.label: Phase E: Graft
nodes.rationale: Fold each graft in by hand so the result stays coherent under one mental model. Don't paste mechanically.

nodes.label: Phase F: Verify
nodes.rationale: If verification finds a problem the arena missed, either Phase A was wrong or a candidate caught it and the graft was missed. Don't paper over it.

nodes.label: Arena Skill
nodes.rationale: Spawn N parallel candidates at the same task, pick a base, graft the strongest parts of the losers into it, for when one attempt at a non-trivial artifact would lock in the wrong shape.

nodes.label: Audit (web)
nodes.rationale: A code-level audit documents measurable, verifiable issues for other commands to fix rather than fixing them in place.

nodes.label: Audit (native)
nodes.rationale: Native audits read from source because no browser tooling or impeccable detect applies; the report skeleton mirrors the web audit so the two stay in sync.

nodes.label: Plan and asset review
nodes.rationale: A painted region planned as code is the most expensive mistake a comp-led build makes, so the user reviews plates and the production plan before any page code exists.

nodes.label: Craft floor
nodes.rationale: The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. A pinned brief or committed visual world overrides it except for lines marked as bans.

nodes.label: Generate (live fast lane)
nodes.rationale: The lane saves time on plumbing only; the variants are planned, written, and accepted exactly as a live session does.

nodes.label: Hooks (design detector)
nodes.rationale: The hook is a mechanical pass that never blocks an edit; the reflexes no scanner catches live in craft-floor.md.

nodes.label: Live mode setup
nodes.rationale: One-time project setup kept out of the per-session hot path; CSP allowances stay development-only so a deployed production site is never weakened.

nodes.label: land.mjs
nodes.rationale: Runs gh with NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR=0/CLICOLOR off and strips escapes before parsing, because gh colourises JSON when the terminal forces colour.

nodes.label: readTracing
nodes.rationale: Opens a finished trace file read-only where it lies and copies only a file a live session still holds, so a 15 GB trace can be scored on an 11 GB-free disk.

nodes.label: Hardening card
nodes.rationale: Prerequisite cost work and widened card attribution belong on the hardening card because they change every historical scorecard.

nodes.label: JUL-310 card
nodes.rationale: Todd approved the card on 1 Nov 2026; this build does the four criteria only because the metrics prerequisite (cache-read pricing, subagent usage recording) is not delivered.

nodes.label: JUL-316 practice card
nodes.rationale: No issued practice card existed, so the practice run creates one; the sweep and the machine both key on a card id.

nodes.label: Record pull request #420
nodes.rationale: Main is protected by a ruleset, so the machine opens its own pull request for the record and retro, waits for checks, and merges it.

nodes.label: docs/practice/README.md
nodes.rationale: Stays in the repository as evidence; deleting it would delete the practice run's proof.

nodes.label: Glycemic load
nodes.rationale: Low at 10 or under, medium to 19, high at 20 and over; the badge colour follows.

nodes.label: Ingredient line
nodes.rationale: The written line is the truth; the parsed parts are only the understanding.

nodes.label: Nutrition panel
nodes.rationale: Always an estimate, worked out on the device from the ingredient parts; tapping it lets you fix a wrongly matched ingredient.

nodes.label: Score
nodes.rationale: Protein and fibre raise it; saturated fat, added sugar, and sodium lower it. A '~' in front means an estimate.

nodes.label: Nutrition panel (product capability)
nodes.rationale: Always an estimate.

nodes.label: Recipe (product capability)
nodes.rationale: Stored as written; scaling, conversions, total time and nutrition are worked out on display.

nodes.label: Cursor-only features skipped in Claude Code
nodes.norm_label: cursor-only features skipped in claude code
nodes.rationale: Claude Code has no Cursor Automations, Bugbot, Cursor cloud agents, or built-in PR tool, so a step needing one is skipped with a one-line note and the run continues rather than stopping or retrying.

nodes.label: Cursor to Claude Code model mapping
nodes.norm_label: cursor to claude code model mapping
nodes.rationale: Claude Code's model field takes only opus, sonnet, haiku, fable, so non-Claude slugs are omitted and the agent runs on the session model.

nodes.label: Cursor to Claude Code path mapping
nodes.norm_label: cursor to claude code path mapping
nodes.rationale: Claude Code never reads .mdc files, and the plugin ships the skills, docs/guide/ and README.md locally, so the local copy is read and never fetched.

nodes.label: setup-pstack in Claude Code
nodes.rationale: Claude Code loads every .md file in ~/.claude/rules/ into each new session, so setup-pstack writes its rule there instead of CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.

nodes.label: Cursor to Claude Code subagent field mapping
nodes.norm_label: cursor to claude code subagent field mapping
nodes.rationale: readonly: true maps to the Explore subagent, which keeps Bash, so the brief must also say not to edit files and git status is checked afterward.

nodes.label: Cursor to Claude Code tool mapping
nodes.norm_label: cursor to claude code tool mapping
nodes.rationale: The Skill tool refuses most pstack skills, so running another pstack skill means reading its SKILL.md and following it.

nodes.label: pstack in Claude Code
nodes.rationale: pstack skills use Cursor names, so in Claude Code this file is read once per session and each Cursor name is mapped with the tables; fields the tool schema rejects are dropped rather than passed.

nodes.label: ~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md
nodes.rationale: Claude Code loads it into every new session, so its role lines are already in context; if the file or a role's line is missing, the skill's default slug is used.

nodes.label: Aborting an in-flight session
nodes.rationale: Use live-poll --reply error rather than live-accept --discard because --discard is a pure file mutator the browser never sees, leaving the bar stuck on dots.

nodes.label: No Comments
nodes.rationale: A keep survives only with proof it is about something we cannot change; correctness or safety suppressions stay actionable MUST KILLs.

nodes.label: /reflect
nodes.rationale: Not used routinely because it produces mostly prose edits.

nodes.label: Bug marks
nodes.rationale: A style attribute wins over a normal CSS rule, so mark rules use !important.

nodes.label: Pele CSS variables
nodes.rationale: Pele ignores Mermaid theme and themeVariables, so colors are set with --pele-* CSS variables.

nodes.label: Render a chart
nodes.rationale: Pele's defaults are smaller than a chart of 500 states can be, so render is called with larger limits.

nodes.label: ADR Search
nodes.rationale: Architectural decision records often live in docs/adr/ or similar and capture out-of-band rationale.

nodes.label: Co-change Signal
nodes.rationale: Related files modified in the same commits can reveal context not stated in the commit message.

nodes.label: Related Tests
nodes.rationale: Test names and assertions often encode the edge cases that motivated a change.

nodes.label: Code Archaeology Playbook
nodes.rationale: The most trustworthy source, tied directly to the code and the most complete; everything that went through the repo should be here.

nodes.label: ADR 0005
nodes.rationale: Says the OVH server never hosts the app; a small checker is not the app, but the choice should be explicit.

nodes.label: Adversarial review
nodes.rationale: Done by a different model maker than the builder's so the review tries to break the work rather than confirm it.

nodes.label: Evidence
nodes.rationale: No Evidence means not done.

nodes.label: Plan
nodes.rationale: Approved automatically and saved in the pull request so both reviewers can check the work against it.

nodes.label: Proof
nodes.rationale: Any source change makes it stale.

nodes.label: Proof story
nodes.rationale: A card that needs more than one drive to prove is too big and splits.

nodes.label: Shipping verdict
nodes.rationale: Left by an agent that did not write the code, after running the change the way Todd uses it; CI stays red without a PASS on the pull request's current head.

nodes.label: Unknown
nodes.rationale: Settled by research or a prototype before triage.

nodes.label: machine/remediation/builder.mjs
nodes.rationale: The builder harness opens the project's own store because that is where the thread that made the change lives; a review harness gets its own LibSQL store under the run folder.

nodes.label: machine/remediation/run.mjs
nodes.rationale: Rounds that already posted are carried forward from record.json, so a crash between two reviews cannot post the first determination twice.

nodes.label: machine/remediation/workflow.mjs
nodes.rationale: Each step reads the record and returns it unchanged when it does not apply, so a first review that passes walks the chain without waking anybody.

nodes.label: MAX_REVIEWS = 2
nodes.rationale: Two failures in a row get a root cause instead of a third try.

nodes.label: machine/remediation/workflow.test.mjs
nodes.rationale: Needs the installed Mastra Code program like Shipping does; a runner without the program reports those rounds as skipped and names the missing packages.

nodes.label: machine/shipping/workflow.mjs
nodes.rationale: Reused rather than copied so a determination looks the same on both machines; it also holds the clock that ends a review that has not answered after twenty minutes.

nodes.label: One harness alive at a time
nodes.norm_label: one harness alive at a time
nodes.rationale: Mastra's observability database takes a process-wide lock, so the machine boots one harness, stops it, and only then boots the next. The workflow's own state lives in a separate LibSQL store so it survives a crash without competing with either harness.

nodes.label: Prove It Works
nodes.rationale: Unverified work has unknown correctness. Indirect verification feels cheaper than direct observation, but acting on a wrong inference costs far more than checking the source.

nodes.label: Sequence Work Into Verifiable Units
nodes.rationale: A break caught at the unit that caused it is cheap to localize. A break caught after a batch is buried, and you have already built further on a broken base.

nodes.label: Steer with principle names
nodes.rationale: Principles are steered by name rather than invoked: each name points at a complete rule the agent has already read, so one phrase redirects the work more precisely than a paragraph of instructions. A principle citation with no decision behind it means the agent named the rule without applying it.

nodes.label: /poteto-mode
nodes.rationale: Reads the principle index at the start of every multi-step task, applies the ones the task triggers, and names each applied principle in its reply along with the decision it changed.

nodes.label: Make it yours
nodes.rationale: Start smaller than you think: prompt plainly, watch where agents fail, and add a skill or check only when the same failure shows up twice.

nodes.label: /automate-me
nodes.rationale: You don't describe your style, because the skill reads it out of your history.

nodes.label: /correct
nodes.rationale: Fixes belong in the repo, not in the next prompt. Options are ranked by how well they hold: make the mistake impossible with architecture, block it with types or a lint/CI check, catch it with a test, and only last write it down as a doc or agent rule — because nothing fails when an agent skips a rule. Human review is deliberately not on the list.

nodes.label: /make-bot-ui
nodes.rationale: A server on your machine holds the webhook's sender key, so the key never reaches the browser or the chat.

nodes.label: Authoring or modifying a skill playbook
nodes.norm_label: authoring or modifying a skill playbook
nodes.rationale: Agent-facing prose has a higher bar than human prose, because an unhelpful sentence becomes an instruction some future agent follows.

nodes.label: Eval playbook
nodes.rationale: Built around the observer effect: an agent that knows it's being evaluated behaves differently, so candidates get organic-looking tasks in sanitized directories and never see each other.

nodes.label: Build the Lever
nodes.rationale: If a script can do a step the same way every time, use the script and save agents for the judgment calls.

nodes.label: Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs
nodes.norm_label: migrate callers then delete legacy apis

nodes.label: Test Behavior, Not Implementation
nodes.rationale: Asserting observable behavior makes a test fail when that behavior breaks and survive a change to the internals.

nodes.label: /reflect
nodes.rationale: Approve a proposal only if it would change a future decision; one weird session is an anecdote, not a rule.

nodes.label: /technical-writing
nodes.rationale: Goal is prose a tired engineer understands on the first read: pick the document mode first, then work sentence by sentence.

nodes.label: Reflect
nodes.rationale: Skill changes affect every future agent in the org, so accepted edits are presented and approved rather than auto-applied.

nodes.label: Experience Mode
nodes.rationale: The visitor is inside the work itself; the artifact leads from the first viewport and the interface recedes.

nodes.label: Persuade Mode
nodes.rationale: The visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing — earn attention and action.

nodes.label: Principles
nodes.rationale: Each principle is a leaf skill read in full when applied, so only principles whose leaf was read this session may be cited.

nodes.label: Authoring or modifying a skill
nodes.rationale: When in doubt, delete. Keep only prose that changes a decision, and point at structural sources instead of restating them.

nodes.label: Merge Frontier
nodes.rationale: The lowest unmerged PR is the only one that matters until it merges; upstack fixes wait so the frontier's checks are not restarted.

nodes.label: Babysit Modes (drive, background, threads-only, check)
nodes.rationale: Declaring a mode up front fixes the stop condition and whether the loop blocks; undeclared defaults to drive, while small or docs-only PRs get check.

nodes.label: Babysit Playbook
nodes.rationale: Replaces Cursor's built-in babysit skill for these requests so matching requests do not route there; landing or shipping is handled by the shipping playbook, which begins where babysitting ends.

nodes.label: GPU Acceleration
nodes.rationale: Use transform and opacity for reliable movement, but allow blur, filters, masks, clip paths, shadows, and color shifts when they create meaningful polish.

nodes.label: Performance Bottleneck
nodes.rationale: Measure before and after. Optimizing without a measurement spends effort on things that do not matter.

nodes.label: will-change
nodes.rationale: Use will-change sparingly for known expensive operations; using it everywhere creates new layers and uses memory.

nodes.label: OffscreenCanvas
nodes.rationale: Render in a Worker thread so the main thread stays free while complex visuals render in the background.

nodes.label: Performance Rules (60fps target)
nodes.rationale: Target 60fps; if dropping below 50, simplify. Lazy-initialize heavy resources, pause off-screen rendering, and test on real mid-range devices.

nodes.label: Progressive Enhancement
nodes.rationale: Every technique must degrade gracefully; the experience without the enhancement must still be good.

nodes.label: Propose Before Building
nodes.rationale: This command has the highest potential to misfire; skipping the direction-selection step risks building something embarrassing that needs to be thrown away.

nodes.label: Scroll-Driven Animations
nodes.rationale: CSS-only, no JS; always provide a static fallback because Firefox support is flag-only.

nodes.label: Verify in the Browser
nodes.rationale: Ambitious effects rarely work on the first try; an effect that technically runs can still stutter, ease wrong, or land on the wrong frame.

nodes.label: Virtual Scrolling
nodes.rationale: Render only visible rows for tables/lists with tens of thousands of items.

nodes.label: Web Workers
nodes.rationale: Move computation off the main thread to avoid jank.

nodes.label: WebGL
nodes.rationale: Use for effects CSS can't express.

nodes.label: WebGPU
nodes.rationale: Next-gen GPU compute, more powerful than WebGL; always fall back to WebGL2.

nodes.label: how skill (companion)
nodes.rationale: why answers what forces led to the code's shape; how answers what the code does and how it works.

nodes.label: why skill
nodes.rationale: Spawns are generalPurpose with readonly false because readonly/Ask mode strips MCP access, which disables the MCP-backed investigators and the synthesizer's citation spot-checks.

nodes.label: Datadog Logs
nodes.rationale: Log searches must be narrowed by service, tag, and time window aggressively, aggregating with analyze_datadog_logs rather than dumping raw logs.

nodes.label: Datadog Metrics
nodes.rationale: A metric's presence is itself evidence that someone thought the number worth watching.

nodes.label: Datadog Monitors & Alerts
nodes.rationale: A monitor firing on a threshold is direct evidence the team worried about that threshold, and the watched threshold is frequently the answer to why code is clamped at N.

nodes.label: Datadog Telemetry
nodes.rationale: Datadog holds the runtime record of what actually happened in production, as opposed to what was planned or discussed.

nodes.label: Bounded prompt batch budget
nodes.rationale: An oversized item fails the verdict closed with evidence.

nodes.label: Install file list completeness
nodes.rationale: A clean-install check must prove no unresolved local import before check/build.

nodes.label: Integrity checks protecting approval and merge
nodes.norm_label: integrity checks protecting approval and merge

nodes.label: Re-read mutable revision after deciding agent finishes
nodes.norm_label: re-read mutable revision after deciding agent finishes
nodes.rationale: A change landed mid-decision cannot be approved under a stale result.

nodes.label: Production check measures the real artifact
nodes.norm_label: production check measures the real artifact
nodes.rationale: An unknown measurement is not reported as zero.

nodes.label: Scheduled operational action runs the real feature
nodes.norm_label: scheduled operational action runs the real feature
nodes.rationale: A read-only check behind a flag that claims the feature is configured is not sufficient.

nodes.label: Verdict reads the whole record
nodes.rationale: A skipped reviewable file fails the verdict closed.

nodes.rationale: Free while capacity lasts

nodes.label: Glyph Cluster
nodes.rationale: Free while the stealth preview lasts

nodes.label: Laguna S 2.1
nodes.rationale: Free while capacity lasts

nodes.label: machine/flow/models.mjs
nodes.rationale: The Lead model is read from its independent setting and routed through its account provider.

nodes.label: machine/flow/run.mjs
nodes.rationale: Answers a waiting card, reads a run and writes its cost; it deliberately offers no way to start a run.

nodes.label: machine/flow/workflow.mjs
nodes.rationale: Holds the order of the stages, the loops and the one place a card waits.

nodes.label: scripts/julia-agents.mjs
nodes.rationale: Runs a machine command with the Julia keys it needs.

nodes.label: scripts/machine-programs.mjs
nodes.rationale: Generates and checks the machine programs list so the list cannot go stale.

nodes.label: Machine programs list
nodes.rationale: The fingerprint is the file's sha256, so the staleness check catches a change of any size, not only a change to the sentence beside it; a pull request that changes a program must update the list in the same pull request.

nodes.label: Core palette (green / terracotta)
nodes.rationale: Which green / terracotta is canonical is a decision for the rebuild; the live app uses both pairs.

nodes.label: SCORE / GL badge
nodes.rationale: The tilde prefix on the score (e.g. ~1) means the value is estimated; hovering reveals a title such as "Nutrient Density: ~1/100 | Glycemic Load: 2.7 (low)".

nodes.label: Undefined text-2xs / text-3xs classes
nodes.rationale: The classes are undefined in the shipped CSS, so those sizes are whatever the parent gives; judge from the screenshots (~10 px).

nodes.label: /figure-it-out
nodes.rationale: Designs the run's phases before any code and wires in the decision log, because the work will be reviewed after stepping away.

nodes.label: /ketchup
nodes.rationale: Reads only and gives a quick plain-language status with screenshots and diagrams, plus each call waiting on the user with its pick, evidence, and risk.

nodes.label: /show-me-your-work
nodes.rationale: Makes the run reviewable by recording time, phase, decision, reason, evidence pointer, and result per row, and spawning a reviewer on a different model family.

nodes.label: decision log
nodes.rationale: Decisions the agent makes on its own are recorded here instead of being escalated to Todd.

nodes.label: decisions.tsv
nodes.rationale: Stays local by default; commit it when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result.

nodes.label: Morning Audit
nodes.rationale: Auditing decisions, not re-reading the whole night; read the Attention section first, then the log rows it points at.

nodes.label: History Mining
nodes.rationale: Patterns seen in 2+ slices are high-confidence; lone signals are weak and usually get dropped, to avoid overfitting to one conversation.

nodes.label: Mode Skill
nodes.rationale: A mode skill is not a manual. Only add a section if the user has a specific, non-default rule there.

nodes.label: Workspace-Scoped Transcripts
nodes.rationale: Use only the active workspace's transcript directory; globbing across every project crosses workspace boundaries and reads private chats from unrelated projects.

nodes.label: Automate Me Skill
nodes.rationale: A guided flow for turning the user's working conventions into a skill agents will follow; it sequences other skills rather than replacing them.

nodes.label: Create Formal Verification Skill
nodes.rationale: A test checks the cases someone thought to write; formal verification checks every case in a stated scope. Target the promise where a break harms users and tests rarely reach the case that breaks it, choose the strongest such target rather than the easiest to verify, and let the question choose the tool at the lowest cost.

nodes.label: Default Mode
nodes.rationale: Preserves identity and varies expression within it; right for ~90% of sessions. Wrong-default costs recoverable on-brand variants, while wrong-departure costs unrecoverable off-brand variants.

nodes.label: Departure Mode
nodes.rationale: Triggered only by explicit user redesign intent; a stale critique or old note is not authorization.

nodes.label: Identity Lock
nodes.rationale: Every variant must read as the same brand side by side; absence of DESIGN.md is never an excuse.

nodes.label: Live Session Journal
nodes.rationale: Append-only journal is canonical durable state and replays unacknowledged work after a helper restart.

nodes.label: Params Sidecar
nodes.rationale: Svelte parses `{` in attribute values as an expression, so params go in a sidecar file rather than as an attribute.

nodes.label: Source-Preview Targets
nodes.rationale: Wrapper and variants must be written in ONE edit because a separate scaffold write reloads the framework before the variant write lands and strands the browser at 0/N.

nodes.label: Create Verification Skill
nodes.rationale: The generated skill is written for the next agent, not a human: it will be read cold, mid-task, by an agent that has never seen the app, so every section must be grounded in what the interview of the repo actually found, with no placeholders left.

nodes.label: Create a Note Feature
nodes.rationale: A save status alone is insufficient proof, so the recipe reopens the note from the list to confirm persistence from a second user-facing view.

nodes.label: Notes Verification Map
nodes.rationale: The map is the maintained source for verifying user-facing behavior, so implementation details are kept out: name only user paths, stable handles, required state, commands, and observable proof.

nodes.label: Search Notes Feature
nodes.rationale: Results update after a short debounce, so the recipe waits for the results list or empty status rather than a fixed sleep; the CLI defaults to human-readable output, so --format json is used for stable assertions.

nodes.label: impeccable comp-spec
nodes.rationale: Writes a coordinate grid over the comp and turns a named regions file into a spec carrying each region's box, sampled palette, and medium; --print is the build's reference from here on.

nodes.label: impeccable font-match
nodes.rationale: Type is measured, not guessed: it reads cap height, width class, and weight off the pixels and ranks candidates from a fingerprint index of the Google Fonts catalog; the gate accepts only what font-match wrote, never a hand-written chosen face.

nodes.label: Phase 4: sections
nodes.rationale: The rest of the surface is built inside the spec's system — same corner language, line weights, and palette, and nothing the comp never shows; where the comp does not cover a region it inherits the recorded system.

nodes.label: Phase 1: spec
nodes.rationale: Anything not in the spec does not exist on the page; the script refuses a regions file that leaves comp ink unnamed because what is never named can never be missing. Only three concessions exist: fonts, icon glyphs, and genuine defects in the comp.

nodes.label: Pele renderer
nodes.rationale: Do not use a different renderer unless the user asks for it.

nodes.label: scripts/statechart.ts
nodes.rationale: TypeScript, so it must be run with a runtime that can execute TypeScript; the first run installs TLC and Java with mise and needs the network.

nodes.label: TLC model checker
nodes.rationale: TLC goes past a state that breaks a rule, so the chart shows the states after a bug; after the first break each run stops at 100,000 distinct states so a large model does not run without end.

nodes.label: Statechart
nodes.rationale: Aim for about 20 arrows or fewer, because a busier chart is hard to read; hide steps only when the chart stays reachable and every state with a step out keeps an arrow. Never weaken a rule to make it hold.

nodes.label: check-pstack-pin.mjs
nodes.rationale: Fails when an installed pstack file differs from the mirror, when @mastra/code-sdk is not exact, or when a local patch mechanism exists.

nodes.label: mastracode program
nodes.rationale: Pinned to 0.47.1 with @mastra/code-sdk 1.14.0; the TUI's update to 0.48.0 is declined while the machine stays on the pinned SDK.

nodes.label: pstack
nodes.rationale: Installed at commit fad8d01588a1b1ae803f87c8a1e0de79e28cffec (version 0.15.32); three extra trees (Benny automation skills, docs/, README.md, LICENSE) were copied manually because the documented install does not copy them.

nodes.label: Device
nodes.rationale: Screen preferences and the current cook-mode step belong to the device, not to a person.

nodes.label: Front door
nodes.rationale: The only way into Julia; there is no public part.

nodes.label: Household account
nodes.rationale: Julia never distinguishes between the two accepted Google accounts; being signed in with either means being in the household.

nodes.label: Installed Julia
nodes.rationale: The expected way to use Julia on a phone and the kitchen tablet, and the way share-to-Julia reaches it; on the desktop Julia is a Chrome tab.

nodes.label: Journey
nodes.rationale: The unit the spec is written in and the unit Todd accepts.

nodes.label: Lab
nodes.rationale: Online only; one Lab conversation at a time, remembered on the device.

nodes.label: Riff
nodes.rationale: The outcome is a new recipe; the original is never changed.

nodes.label: Spark
nodes.rationale: Becomes part of the kept recipe's source.

nodes.label: Variation
nodes.rationale: Each of the four cards is built from the pairing data a different way: Classic, Adventurous, Chemistry, Balanced.

nodes.label: Harness
nodes.rationale: pstack was written for Cursor, so Cursor-specific instructions are mapped onto other harnesses rather than rewritten.

nodes.label: Ketchup Video
nodes.rationale: Rendering the video outside the repo is the one exception to ketchup's read-only rule.

nodes.label: Maintain a Formal Verification Skill
nodes.rationale: A check that keeps passing on a stale description is the dangerous case because it looks like a proof; this skill handles changes that skipped the project-local verify skill.

nodes.label: Maintain a Verification Skill
nodes.rationale: The unit of rigor is the feature, not every sentence: cover every feature file from source and exercise every feature live without terminalising every bullet.

nodes.label: Off-peak / Peak Pricing Schedule

nodes.label: docs/adr/

nodes.label: docs/agents/work-execution.md
nodes.rationale: The delivery route.
