nodes.rationale: The culinary domain model for this single-context repository.

nodes.label: impeccable embed-prompt
nodes.rationale: Keeps raster provenance: the exact generation prompt for a produced raster, the origin for a sourced or pre-existing one.

nodes.label: impeccable-asset-producer agent
nodes.rationale: Shipped asset producer spawned with the spec path so parallel subagents can produce all plates; without subagents the plates are produced in-thread.

nodes.label: Phase 2: plates
nodes.rationale: A crop of the comp is a reference, never a shipping pixel; page code waits for this gate because a page written before its plates exist is a page that draws its material in CSS.

nodes.label: Spring Physics
nodes.rationale: Natural motion with mass, tension, and damping instead of cubic-bezier.

nodes.label: Engine Binary Checksums
nodes.rationale: Every engine download is verified against this file so launchers, the npm shim, install and fetch-engine all trust the same pinned digests.

nodes.label: Interrogate
nodes.rationale: A finding survives only when a run proves it, so style, naming, structure and future-risk observations are excluded.

nodes.label: Tailscale Tailnet Hosting
nodes.rationale: Agents on one computer share a single Tailscale node, so a second hostname is never created on a node that is already online.

nodes.label: Make a Bot UI
nodes.rationale: The sender key stays on the server so it never reaches the browser, chat, or the skill text.

nodes.label: Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs
nodes.norm_label: migrate callers then delete legacy apis

nodes.label: Never Block on the Human
nodes.rationale: Since code changes are reversible and reviewable, a wrong decision usually costs less than blocking.

nodes.label: Outcome-Oriented Execution
nodes.rationale: Keeping every intermediate step fully stable often creates temporary compatibility code that becomes long-lived debt.

nodes.label: list (in-memory shopping list)
nodes.rationale: In-memory only; nothing is persisted so a reload clears it.

nodes.label: listen (hands-free)
nodes.rationale: A 12s idle timer ends the session gracefully if the user goes quiet.

nodes.label: openListening
nodes.rationale: A 2.5s silence timer auto-advances to the confirm step so the user need not press Done.

nodes.label: renderA (Hold to talk)
nodes.rationale: Items land immediately with editable chips so the user can fix mistakes after the fact rather than confirming before.

nodes.label: renderB (Listen, then confirm)
nodes.rationale: A confirm sheet gates additions so nothing touches the list until the user approves the parsed items.

nodes.label: renderC (Hands-free conversation)
nodes.rationale: Continuous listen/speak loop with spoken readback and removal by voice, ending on 'that's all' or a 12s idle timeout.

nodes.label: say (hands-free)
nodes.rationale: Recognition is aborted before speaking to avoid the mic hearing Julia's own voice.

nodes.label: show (variant switcher)
nodes.rationale: Tears down the previous variant before rendering the next and syncs the choice into the URL query string.

nodes.label: showHeard
nodes.rationale: Surfaces the transcript plus per-item chips with undo so a mis-heard batch can be corrected or reverted in one tap.

nodes.label: VARIANTS registry
nodes.rationale: Three interaction models (hold-to-talk, listen-then-confirm, hands-free conversation) are registered so the switcher can render and compare them side by side.

nodes.label: Typed Fallback Input
nodes.rationale: Always available so the variant can be exercised on desktop or when the microphone is denied.

nodes.label: Browser Speech Recognition API
nodes.rationale: Uses the browser's built-in speech recognition (Chrome, Edge, Safari); browsers cannot listen continuously, so a wake word is out of scope.

nodes.label: poll_sql_result
nodes.rationale: Poll with poll_sql_result when a statement_id is returned rather than re-running the query.

nodes.label: Undefined --font-ui / --font-display variables
nodes.rationale: Referenced by globals.css and the Lab page's inline styles but never defined, so Lab descriptive text and the Edit profile button fall back to system sans-serif; treat that as a bug, not a design choice.

nodes.label: Rehearsal copy
nodes.rationale: Real Julia is never involved.

nodes.label: Test data
nodes.rationale: Set up once and shared by every rehearsal copy; never Real Julia's data.

nodes.label: UAT
nodes.rationale: Only things a user would do; technical checking is the robot's job and happens before UAT.

nodes.label: Benny Automation Pack
nodes.rationale: A dormant automation pack for Slack issue reports: one automation triages each report, another reproduces confirmed bugs and may prepare a small draft fix.

nodes.label: Impeccable Manual Edit Applier
nodes.rationale: Runs the role inline because the harness has no subagent capability; the parent live thread owns polling and protocol replies while this role owns source edits only.

nodes.label: Document (DESIGN.md)
nodes.rationale: Tokens in the frontmatter are normative and prose provides context, so AI agents generating new screens stay on-brand.

nodes.label: Author motion as material
nodes.rationale: Give the page the form's native motion once, orchestrated, rather than scattered hover effects; bound expensive effects and keep content visible by default.

nodes.label: Build the form's web leverage
nodes.rationale: When the chosen world names a technique (canvas, WebGL, view transitions, generative motion), build the technique itself, not a static imitation of it.

nodes.label: Animated Data Transitions
nodes.rationale: Morph between chart states rather than replacing.

nodes.label: GPU-Accelerated Charts
nodes.rationale: Canvas or WebGL-rendered data visualization for datasets too large for SVG/DOM.

nodes.label: Device APIs
nodes.rationale: Use sparingly and always with user permission.

nodes.label: Web Audio API
nodes.rationale: Requires user gesture to start; never add sound without explicit user opt-in.

nodes.label: Fix Root Causes
nodes.rationale: A symptom fix hides the evidence and leaves the fault free to surface somewhere else. Each one makes the system harder to reason about, because the code now carries a workaround for a bug that nobody named.

nodes.label: Make Operations Idempotent
nodes.rationale: Commands, lifecycle operations, and processing loops run where crashes, restarts, and retries are normal. If partial state changes the next run's outcome, every restart becomes a debugging session.

nodes.label: Handling Contradicting Evidence
nodes.rationale: Surface both sources with citations rather than picking the one that fits a tidier narrative.

nodes.label: The Sycophancy Trap
nodes.rationale: A hypothesis embedded in the user's question is a prompt for investigation, not a conclusion to validate.

nodes.label: Coding standards
nodes.rationale: Grows one line at a time, added in the same pull request as the fix that showed the rule was needed.

nodes.label: Correct Skill
nodes.rationale: Assume every contributor is an agent that sees only the files it opened, copies the nearest example, and takes the shortest path that compiles, so the repo must be designed so a change that looks right from one file is right for the whole repo. Fix each mistake class at the highest level that works — architecture, then types, then a lint whose error names the fix, then a test, and docs last — because nothing fails when an agent skips docs.

nodes.label: Critique
nodes.rationale: Two independent assessments are required so deterministic detector output never anchors the design judgment; a degraded single-context run must announce itself.

nodes.label: Author the assets; never substitute chrome
nodes.norm_label: author the assets; never substitute chrome
nodes.rationale: Gradients, glass, generic icon tiles, and many-vertex clip-path polygons where an authored asset belongs are the gap wearing chrome; content is authorable, claims are labelable, no section is omittable.

nodes.label: machine/flow
nodes.rationale: Must keep the stock shape: no old stage, no library outside the allowed set, no unreachable piece, no timer or retry loop, no hand-built progress file, no comment that switches a guard off.

nodes.label: machine/guards/guard.test.mjs
nodes.rationale: Plants one violation per kind and fails if a rule stops catching it.

nodes.label: node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js

nodes.label: scripts/check-agent-brief.mjs
nodes.rationale: Flags an acceptance criterion that names a specific model instead of a kind of model.

nodes.label: scripts/check-agent-links.mjs
nodes.rationale: Checks that current agent-read files point only at paths that exist.

nodes.label: scripts/check-branch-pr.mjs
nodes.rationale: Audits GitHub branches and open pull requests in CI so every branch except main has an open PR to main.

nodes.label: scripts/check-skill-names.mjs
nodes.rationale: Rejects duplicate frontmatter names so skill names stay unique across installed catalogs.

nodes.label: scripts/julia-agents.mjs
nodes.rationale: Wraps commands that need Julia keys.

nodes.label: scripts/machine-programs.mjs
nodes.rationale: Fails when a listed program's file changed, when a listed program is gone, or when machine/flow holds a program the list never names.

nodes.label: scripts/trace-store.mjs
nodes.rationale: `status` answers the trace-store size question.

nodes.label: .agents/skills/
nodes.rationale: Skills are edited in the folder they live in.

nodes.label: .claude/skills/
nodes.rationale: Skills are edited in the folder they live in.

nodes.label: .artifacts/flow
nodes.rationale: Studio run state is kept here while other disposable artifacts go under the scratch directory.

nodes.label: Done means a record
nodes.rationale: A build is done when a run produced a record, not when the builder says it passed; the builder never runs the machine that judges the work, and a failed verdict is a result on the card rather than the builder's failure.

nodes.label: Enforced rules table
nodes.rationale: Each rule is paired with a script or CI check so the rule is enforced mechanically rather than by convention.

nodes.label: pstack full-autonomy grant
nodes.rationale: Pre-approves deleting server files from finished work, changing server configuration and schedulers, and merging to main once required checks pass, so work is not blocked on approvals.

nodes.label: Graphify
nodes.rationale: Two knowledge graphs are queried before grepping or reading files, so agents ask the graph first.

nodes.label: guard:flow
nodes.rationale: Runs ESLint and dependency-cruiser on machine/flow as the one CI guard check, keeping the workflow folder in its stock shape.

nodes.label: Inverse pyramid
nodes.rationale: Corrections are fixed as high in the pyramid as they will go; a written rule is the last resort.

nodes.label: ~/.local/state/julia-scratch
nodes.rationale: Disposable checkouts, copies and run artifacts go here even when a skill suggests a different temporary path.

nodes.label: machine program list
nodes.rationale: Names every program that begins a card or carries a stage, and must stay current.

nodes.label: Mastra Studio run form
nodes.rationale: A card begins in Mastra Studio's run form and nowhere else; no script starts one.

nodes.label: Next.js agent rules block
nodes.rationale: Written and re-added by `next dev`; removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change, so committing it keeps the tree clean.

nodes.label: pstack models file
nodes.rationale: A specific model lives in the pstack models file and in the dated decision that chose it, so rules and acceptance criteria name only a kind of model.

nodes.label: retro skill
nodes.rationale: Run on each merged slice's session and its fixes shipped in one PR with a plain-English list for Todd; the next slice does not wait for that PR.

nodes.label: Todd
nodes.rationale: Todd decides what Julia does for the household and gives UAT; everything else is decided by the agent and recorded in the decision log, so he is only brought decisions he alone can make.

nodes.label: trace store
nodes.rationale: Every session writes its own trace file and a daily trace-fold timer folds finished files into the archive beside them, so prompt payloads leave the disk without anyone remembering; retro must not touch it.

nodes.label: UAT
nodes.rationale: Todd gives UAT; a card that changes something he uses is not finished without his yes.

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.rationale: Owns code, commits, pull requests and CI.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md — Julia rulebook
nodes.rationale: Declared as the whole rulebook for the Julia repo; pstack builds and proves, and every correction should be fixed as high in the inverse pyramid as it will go, with a written rule as the last resort.

nodes.label: graphify-out/graph.json
nodes.rationale: Holds the Julia code, Julia docs and pstack skills graph; rebuilt after each commit through installed git hooks.

nodes.label: graphify-out/mastra/graph.json
nodes.rationale: Holds the installed Mastra documentation graph; needs the commands in docs/agents/graphify.md after Mastra upgrades.

nodes.label: node_modules/next/dist/docs/
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes, so the version-matched guide must be read before writing any code.

nodes.label: Disposition: rebuild
nodes.rationale: Fidelity failed wholesale, not in patches: re-derive the named regions, produce the named assets, and send the result back for a fresh full review, never a verdict pass.

nodes.label: Phase 5: motion
nodes.rationale: The signature interaction, reveals, and motion are orchestrated once rather than scattered.

nodes.label: Prove, don't claim
nodes.rationale: Show the subject doing its job with specifics a competitor could not copy-paste; demonstration data is authored at full fidelity and labelled synthetic, so claims stay uninventable.

nodes.label: Use real, verified imagery
nodes.rationale: Search for the subject's physical object rather than the category; one decisive photo beats five mediocre ones, and stock URLs must be verified to resolve.

nodes.label: Pace the scroll like a studio
nodes.norm_label: pace the scroll like a studio
nodes.rationale: Vary density, scale, image, motion, and quiet inside one grammar; a dense passage earns a quiet one, and the page ends anchored by a real close.

nodes.label: CSS @property
nodes.rationale: Register custom CSS properties with types, enabling animation of gradients, colors, and complex values CSS can't normally interpolate.

nodes.label: SVG Filter Chains
nodes.rationale: Displacement maps, turbulence, morphology for organic distortion effects; CSS-animatable.

nodes.label: View Transitions API
nodes.rationale: Closest thing to native FLIP animations; shared element morphing between states.

nodes.label: WebAssembly (WASM)
nodes.rationale: Near-native performance for computation-heavy features.

nodes.label: Web Animations API
nodes.rationale: JavaScript-driven animations with the performance of CSS; composable, cancellable, reversible.

nodes.label: impeccable generate-image
nodes.rationale: API fallback for plate production when the harness-native image tool is unavailable.

nodes.label: Pause safely
nodes.rationale: You own a clean stop; leave a checkpoint a cold-start agent can resume from. Explicit only — on 'keep going' or 'don't stop', do not pause.

nodes.label: Boundary Discipline
nodes.rationale: Scattered validation is noisy, redundant, and gives a false sense of safety. Keep logic out of framework wiring so it can be tested without the framework.

nodes.label: Sharpen
nodes.rationale: A deeper version of a task, not a bigger one: start from raw material rather than what has already been digested, and leave choices that belong to the user open instead of deciding them.

nodes.label: Avoid Rationalization
nodes.rationale: Code that makes sense today may have been written for reasons that no longer apply; do not retrofit a clean rationale onto messy history.

nodes.label: Investigator Code Anchor
nodes.rationale: Gives each investigator the target files, symbols, seed commits, PR numbers, and ticket IDs so it can orient its search.

nodes.label: Logging good enough to find a root cause
nodes.norm_label: logging good enough to find a root cause
nodes.rationale: Temporary debugging or a silent non-zero exit is insufficient; each connection between services records its own trace.

nodes.label: Old machine systemd units
nodes.rationale: Stopped and disabled with reset-failed; unit files and code remain in place.

nodes.label: Server-owned tests
nodes.rationale: The worker was run once by hand with its service PATH because the julia-server-tests timer is off; the timer stays off.

nodes.label: Parking lot
nodes.rationale: Read at every retro and at each milestone boundary.

nodes.label: impeccable concept-seed
nodes.rationale: The roll is what keeps every run from converging on the category default; writing artifact code before the script has run and its assignment acknowledged is a contract violation.

nodes.label: impeccable serve-question
nodes.rationale: Daemonizes and prints a page URL and key so the decision is presented visually rather than in chat; never start a second server or fall back to chat mid-round.

nodes.label: buildPath Setting
nodes.rationale: A flipped value binds that session only and is never written back, except when a Persuade or Experience surface in a project recording no buildPath at all earns one question after the round closes.

nodes.label: build-phase state machine
nodes.rationale: Gates measure the screen against the comp rather than relying on the builder's memory; exit 2 means the gate failed and printed why, and nothing may be written for a later phase while an earlier gate is open.

nodes.label: AI-Interface Calibration Defaults
nodes.rationale: If someone could guess your aesthetic from the category alone, or from category-plus-avoidance, the self-check failed and the work must be reworked until neither answer is obvious.

nodes.label: Catalog Worlds
nodes.rationale: Catalog worlds are working systems, not mood references: a surviving world carries its palette, material, type, composition, topology, controls, state, and responsive rules into the product.

nodes.label: Code-led Build Path
nodes.rationale: Working screens and documents come out better built than pictured; code-led is not a discount on commitment, the ambition moves into the written contract.

nodes.label: Color Strategy (Restrained / Committed / Full palette / Drenched)
nodes.norm_label: color strategy (restrained / committed / full palette / drenched)
nodes.rationale: Pick a color strategy before picking colors; color commits at page scale as fields that own whole regions, and dark or light is never a default but forced by a sentence of physical scene.

nodes.label: Comp-led Build Path
nodes.rationale: Visualizing the locked direction before building is proven to produce the most compositional and ambitious work; the comp is law and non-optional.

nodes.label: Comp-Led Build
nodes.rationale: A locked comp builds comp-led with that comp as the approved comp, discharging visualize.md's three-option round with no second approval point.

nodes.label: Comp Prompt Sidecar
nodes.rationale: Every landed decision comp needs its prompt sidecar written the moment the file is done, so a re-roll's spend front-loads onto the cards read first.

nodes.label: Phase 0: comps
nodes.rationale: Three compositional comps at the surface's own viewport, each with a prompt sidecar; the chosen one's sidecar gets "approved": true, and a start --comp skips this phase because it already happened.

nodes.label: Concept Tournament
nodes.rationale: Derive five to seven materially different structures ordered by resonance, then deal three so the dice break the ranking rut while the user keeps a real choice. Not used for local extensions or precisely specified narrow requests.

nodes.label: Decision Page
nodes.rationale: Presents candidate structures as full cards of equal salience with steer and re-roll so the user locks one; at surface scope every card visualizes composition, not identity, because the world is settled.

nodes.label: Disposition: fix
nodes.rationale: Apply the material fixes in one batch, rebuild once, and recapture the same viewports over the same files; the reviewer's findings are the only list to work from.

nodes.label: Incomplete Brand
nodes.rationale: Preserve confirmed assets and recognizable traits, then expand the system with the user for this surface.

nodes.label: .impeccable/mocks/decision/
nodes.rationale: Holds the generated comps for the decision page, generated after serving, in reading order.

nodes.label: MODE RULES Block
nodes.rationale: Governs every direction, card, and comp for the surface, and wins where it conflicts with shared guidance.

nodes.label: No Visual Authority
nodes.rationale: With no existing visual authority, a new world is created with the user.

nodes.label: IMPECCABLE'S PICK Card
nodes.rationale: One pick card, never two, never a ranked list: a lineup of your candidates hands selection back to a taste function and invites the safest card.

nodes.label: PRESENTATION Block
nodes.rationale: Names the shape of the HTML sketch a card carries and the build path printed for the surface.

nodes.label: QUALITY BAR Cards and Boards
nodes.rationale: They set the craft level the build must reach — finish, commitment, art direction — never the composition; the surface serves this product.

nodes.label: Redesign
nodes.rationale: Preserve product truth, content, function, constraints, and explicit brand commitments; replace the old visual world rather than polishing it. The old look is evidence of what the subject is, not authority over what it becomes.

nodes.label: Re-roll Registers (plain / safer / bolder)
nodes.rationale: The register is the user's steering on the familiar-to-bold axis, never the agent's to pre-select.

nodes.label: The Rut (Category Default and Its Opposite)
nodes.norm_label: the rut (category default and its opposite)
nodes.rationale: The page the category always ships and its predictable opposite are both the rut, kept out of the seven-candidate list.

nodes.label: Seven-Candidate Visual Systems List
nodes.rationale: When more than three of the seven share one material family the derivation stopped at the subject's most obvious artifact; the list must span at least three families.

nodes.label: Standing Exit
nodes.rationale: It is the user's door, never yours: never recommend it, never weigh it against the roll, never let it soften the dealt directions; the counterweights bind the unchosen default, not the chosen one.

nodes.label: Challenger Verdicts (wins / competitive / declined)
nodes.rationale: The verdict informs the user's choice, never pre-empts it; the demoted row is the hand's proof of judgment.

nodes.label: .impeccable/config.json
nodes.rationale: Holds the recorded buildPath default for the project.

nodes.label: .impeccable/config.local.json
nodes.rationale: Gitignored; wins where one machine differs from the team's committed value.

nodes.label: visualize.md
nodes.rationale: Must be loaded before writing the first decision comp prompt; a prompt written before reading it misses every rule there.

nodes.label: PRODUCT.md
nodes.rationale: Durable product context captured by init; missing PRODUCT.md routes a new surface or replacement world through init, then new-work.

nodes.label: PRODUCT.md
nodes.rationale: Owns product truth.

nodes.label: Voice Add Prototype
nodes.rationale: Throwaway prototype exploring what adding to the shopping list by voice should feel like (Linear JUL-18); nothing is saved, reload and it's gone.

nodes.label: Impeccable Asset Producer
nodes.rationale: Production cleanup, not new art direction: the comp was approved as it is, so the role preserves the reference's visual role, silhouette, palette, lighting, material, texture, camera angle and composition rather than redesigning.

nodes.label: Core Rule (Do Not Redesign)
nodes.rationale: Presentation chrome (card transform, shadow, rounded clipping, border, layout) belongs to CSS, so it is removed from the raster; perspective is kept only when it belongs to the object or scene itself.

nodes.label: Decision Comps
nodes.rationale: The parent runs several producers in parallel, one per card, so the file on disk is the deliverable and the decision page is waiting on it: generate first, plan never.

nodes.label: Frame Plate
nodes.rationale: The content seen through a window, doorway or arch is its own image region, so the opening must stay fully transparent with no baked view or glow halo.

nodes.label: Input Contract
nodes.rationale: The spec is the inventory; a second inventory would disagree with the first, so the producer never inventories the comp itself.

nodes.label: needs_parent_review Status
nodes.rationale: After two visual misses on one region the better plate is kept and flagged rather than iterated indefinitely; the producer never self-approves.

nodes.label: Opaque Plate
nodes.rationale: A photograph, full-frame illustration or texture is full-frame by nature, so it stays opaque rather than being cut out.

nodes.label: Output Contract
nodes.rationale: A visual acceptance does not override a failing gate, so the parent verifies plates against the same spec via build-phase advance.

nodes.label: Plate
nodes.rationale: The page draws text, controls, radius, shadow and layout in code; the plate carries only what code cannot draw.

nodes.label: Plates Gate
nodes.rationale: The parent runs the gate after all assets exist, so plates report unscored until a gate score is available.

nodes.label: Review Handoff
nodes.rationale: A parent or automatic visual check is not a substitute for the human checkpoint, so real files and unresolved drift go back to the parent for the user's plan and asset review.

nodes.label: The Job (Plate Production)
nodes.rationale: Crops from the comp are reference grade, never shipping pixels: a shipped crop is how a beautiful comp becomes a blurry site, so each raster region is regenerated at 1.5x or more.

nodes.label: Transparent Cutout
nodes.rationale: An isolated figure, object or line drawing on the page ground must composite over any background, so it ships with a real alpha channel and clear margins, white paint, fine edges and interior holes preserved.

nodes.label: Check 3: Ceiling
nodes.rationale: The QUALITY BAR card governs commitment and finish, never composition.

nodes.label: Check 4: Contract, promise by promise
nodes.rationale: A raw seed key in FORM is itself a material fix: the brief is committed, and the key must not be.

nodes.label: Disposition Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: The word is derived, never felt: recapture on failed evidence, rebuild on the rebuild-directive condition, fix when material_fixes is non-empty, ship only when material_fixes is empty and no row is contradicted or missing.

nodes.label: Check 0: Evidence
nodes.rationale: A viewport nobody captured is a viewport nobody inspected; a verdict derived from a broken capture launders the breakage into an approval, so any invalid capture forces a recapture disposition instead of a matrix.

nodes.label: Check 2: Fidelity
nodes.rationale: The comp is the spec for composition, topology, element inventory, density, lettering character and material, but not a pixel spec for semantics, accessibility or responsive reflow; judging against the contract's summary of the comp would inherit whatever the builder's abstraction dropped.

nodes.label: Check 6: Floor
nodes.rationale: Fidelity to a comp cannot authorize what the craft floor refuses; this check exists because hookless harnesses reach the reviewer with no mechanical findings.

nodes.label: Check 1: Persistence
nodes.rationale: A skipped comp round or unproven hero reproduction outranks craft, because the build then ran from a world description alone.

nodes.label: Check 5: Truth
nodes.rationale: An asset applied at near-zero opacity or buried behind a wash is a compliance token, not a shipped material.

nodes.label: Verdict Pass
nodes.rationale: Post-fix returns are scoring, not re-hunting; the parent's narration of what was fixed is not evidence, and a claimed fix not visible in the recaptures is unresolved.

nodes.label: Impeccable Finish Reviewer
nodes.rationale: This harness has no subagent capability, so the role runs inline: the agent steps out of the finished work, adopts only this file's instructions, and discloses the substitution to the user outside the output contract.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md
nodes.rationale: On a new world DESIGN.md is written after this review by the documenter, so its absence here is not a finding.

nodes.label: Direction Contract (THESIS, OWN-WORLD, STORY, FIRST VIEWPORT, FORM)
nodes.norm_label: direction contract (thesis, own-world, story, first viewport, form)

nodes.label: .impeccable/mocks/ Comp-Round Comps
nodes.rationale: Files under .impeccable/mocks/decision/ are exempt: they are the direction round's dealt hand, produced before any comp round, and imply no approval whatever the build path.

nodes.label: Manual assertions
nodes.rationale: Generated code captures actions but not assertions, so expectations must be added manually.

nodes.label: Action-to-TypeScript generation
nodes.rationale: Every playwright-cli action emits the equivalent Playwright TypeScript, which is the raw material for every test.

nodes.label: Debug/attach workflow (--debug=cli + attach tw-XXXX)
nodes.rationale: Plan, generate and heal all lean on the same mechanic: run the test paused in the background and drive the page interactively.

nodes.label: Seed fixture (tests/fixtures.ts)
nodes.rationale: Pushing navigation into a fixture lets scenario tests reuse it instead of repeating navigation.

nodes.label: Generate phase
nodes.rationale: The live app is the source of truth; editing the spec mid-generation is expected when it is vague or stale.

nodes.label: Heal phase
nodes.rationale: Failures are fixed one at a time because shared state and the single CLI session make parallel fixes fragile; sleeps and networkidle are never acceptable fixes.

nodes.label: Plan phase
nodes.rationale: Always write the spec to a file so generation and healing have a stable, reviewable source of truth.

nodes.label: Seed test
nodes.rationale: A minimal test that lands the page in the state every scenario starts from; --debug=cli pauses inside it, so every planning and generation session begins there.

nodes.label: Semantic (role-based) locators
nodes.rationale: Role-based locators are more resilient than fragile CSS selectors.

nodes.label: Verification Outcomes

nodes.label: Patched Build Measurement

nodes.label: Qualify the Fix Artifact

nodes.label: Hard Safety Rules

nodes.label: Ownership and Fix-Artifact Gates

nodes.rationale: GL = (GI x available carbohydrate) / 100, summed per recipe and divided by servings, matching the Sydney FAQ, Illinois Extension bands and the glossary.

nodes.label: Household Default per Bare Generic Word
nodes.norm_label: household default per bare generic word
nodes.rationale: Bare generic words like flour, oil, cheese and milk resolve to a household default (flour to all-purpose, oil to olive, cheese to cheddar, milk to whole) and stay marked '~' until Todd fixes the match by tapping the panel.

nodes.label: Negligible Ingredient Set

nodes.label: Table A: Nutrition Table (trimmed USDA SR Legacy)
nodes.norm_label: table a: nutrition table (trimmed usda sr legacy)
nodes.rationale: SR Legacy is the workhorse because Foundation Foods has too many holes (only 95 of 395 carry plain energy values, portion weights on 83); SR Legacy is frozen but wheat flour and olive oil have not changed since 2018, and Foundation Foods can top up individual rows later without changing the design.

nodes.label: Table B: Glycemic Index Table
nodes.rationale: GI only matters where there are carbohydrates to load, so ~200 values plus food-group defaults suffice; taking a couple of hundred measured numbers and citing the 2021 paper per row is citing published measurements, not republishing the tables.

nodes.rationale: Clever matching still needs a hand list for the common words; a bare generic word can always resolve to a row but is wrong-by-design for oil, cheese and dairy unless the household default is right, so such matches are marked '~' until fixed.

nodes.label: Table D: Fallback Portion Weights
nodes.rationale: A handful of generic weights cover the cases where a matched row carries no portion of its own; using them marks the line '~'.

nodes.label: The '~' Estimate Mark Rule
nodes.rationale: '~' means at least one ingredient line that could move the number was worked out by a fallback rather than a match; negligible ingredients (salt, pepper, herbs, spices, water, vinegar, leavening, extracts) never mark the panel because they cannot move the number.

nodes.norm_label: understand the code before changing it
nodes.rationale: Agents fail either by misreading intent or by lacking context; this page addresses the context half, because editing code you don't understand is how subtle regressions ship.

nodes.label: figure-it-out skill
nodes.rationale: Designs the phases of an unattended run so work reviewed later still has structure.

nodes.label: how skill
nodes.rationale: An agent that starts editing without a traced model tends to fix the symptom at the first plausible spot, so /how first is cheaper than the second bug.

nodes.label: in-your-own-words skill
nodes.rationale: Restates the agent's understanding of goals and problem without running a playbook, so a misreading surfaces before any code exists.

nodes.label: Investigation playbook

nodes.label: Opening a PR playbook
nodes.rationale: Already works from a worktree for code changes, so a worktree only needs to be requested when a specific base or location matters.

nodes.label: Session pickup playbook
nodes.rationale: Treats the prior trail as authoritative: reconstructs branch state and decisions, names the resume point, and verifies inherited claims against the original goal instead of re-deriving everything.

nodes.label: Worktree cleanup playbook
nodes.rationale: Classifies every worktree by merge state, uncommitted work, and which chats still touch it; deletes only what that evidence clears and pauses for a human call on anything holding uncommitted work.

nodes.label: recall skill
nodes.rationale: Old chats hold context a fresh agent lacks, so new work on an old topic starts by loading that context first.

nodes.label: sharpen skill
nodes.rationale: Rewrites a prompt deeper but not bigger and leaves the user's choices open; it does not do the task, so the user can review the rewrite before sending it.

nodes.label: show-me-your-work skill
nodes.rationale: Keeps a decision log so an unattended run's choices can be reviewed afterwards.

nodes.label: teach skill
nodes.rationale: An agent that has to explain its work must read the code and back each claim with evidence instead of stating it confidently and moving on.

nodes.label: why skill
nodes.rationale: Reports null results too, because 'nobody wrote down why' is itself an answer; separates direct evidence from inference and hedges when the record is thin.

nodes.label: card-path workflow
nodes.rationale: The run form asks only for card and kind, and the saved state starts empty, so a run started in Studio needs no preparation.

nodes.label: machine/flow/mastra.mjs
nodes.rationale: Holds the Mastra instance, the two stores, and the span processor that stamps every span with the card.

nodes.label: machine/flow/run.mjs
nodes.rationale: After JUL-338 keeps only resume, status and cost; the start command was removed.

nodes.label: machine/flow/schema.mjs
nodes.rationale: One flowData shape every stage takes and returns, plus cardState, the saved state.

nodes.label: machine/flow/start.mjs
nodes.rationale: Assembles a run, starts it, and resumes it.

nodes.label: machine/flow/trace.mjs
nodes.rationale: Mastra's exporter buffers spans, so the command line shuts the instance down before totalling the trace.

nodes.label: machine/flow/workflow.mjs
nodes.rationale: Flow logic may exist only as workflow and agent definitions, each piece of order, state, retry, FAIL count and wait carried by a documented Mastra feature.

nodes.label: unfold mapper
nodes.rationale: A branch's output carries a key for every arm that did not run with undefined under it, so the mapper takes the arm that produced card data instead of reading the object directly.

nodes.label: scripts/check-no-fakes.mjs
nodes.rationale: Keeps machine/flow/ as the one folder allowed a stand-in for an outside service, because the flow's stand-ins are its design.

nodes.label: scripts/machine-programs.mjs
nodes.rationale: --check fails a pull request that changes a machine program without updating the list, making a machine change a reviewable diff.

nodes.label: src/mastra/index.ts
nodes.rationale: Registers the same workflow against the same state store so Mastra Studio shows a run the command line started.

nodes.label: acceptance stage
nodes.rationale: The wait sits two levels deep, not three, because resuming a deeper suspension restarts the outermost suspended step; it re-suspends while resumeData.request differs to refuse stale answers.

nodes.label: scripts/julia-agents.env
nodes.rationale: Maps CMD_API_KEY to the same 1Password item the model registry reads.

nodes.label: scripts/start-machine.mjs
nodes.rationale: Deleted with its test in JUL-338 because a card now starts only in Mastra Studio's run form.

nodes.label: JUL-334 (negative control)
nodes.rationale: Its build step reached for the machine's own harness instead of the workflow engine, which is why it does not count as the pattern.

nodes.label: JUL-338 update
nodes.rationale: A card begins in Studio and the build stage is real; two stand-ins are gone and the command-line start was removed.

nodes.label: Mastra per-run snapshots
nodes.rationale: A run killed while it waits comes back at the same stage.

nodes.label: Mastra Studio
nodes.rationale: A card starts in Studio's run form and nowhere else after JUL-338.

nodes.label: Mastra workflow state (stateSchema/setState)
nodes.rationale: State is part of the saved snapshot, so the FAIL count survives a wait and a resume of the same run.

nodes.label: machine/flow/agents.mjs
nodes.rationale: Four plain agents on the free model with no tools; agent stages retry, deciding stages do not, because a re-run of a deciding stage would count a FAIL twice.

nodes.label: finishBuild stage
nodes.rationale: Writes what the agent wrote into the card's folder and puts the flow data back.

nodes.label: startBuild stage
nodes.rationale: Names the card, counts the round, sets the request id and returns the prompt, because the agent step's contract is {prompt} in and {text} out.

nodes.label: Mastra Code
nodes.rationale: Headless mode validates the -m model id against a cached model catalog (run-mc.js:298); the running session was not restarted because restarting would end the conversation, and each new headless run rereads settings.

nodes.label: Startup model restore from thread metadata
nodes.norm_label: startup model restore from thread metadata
nodes.rationale: The thread's saved model wins over MASTRACODE_MODEL_ID once a thread has a saved model.

nodes.label: stripMastraCodeCustomProviderPrefix
nodes.rationale: The picker strips the mastracode/ prefix from custom-provider ids before showing them; the prefix only appears in the full id used for MASTRACODE_MODEL_ID and headless --model.

nodes.label: COMMANDCODE_API_KEY
nodes.rationale: Must never be printed or committed; the old key was rejected with HTTP 401 and was replaced with the new key from the "Julia agents" vault.

nodes.label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
nodes.rationale: DeepSeek only worked because Mastra Code's built-in list already contained it; the custom entry was supplying the key, not the model.

nodes.label: mastracode resume command
nodes.rationale: resume takes exactly one argument and the TUI has no --model or --thread flag; those flags exist only for headless --prompt runs.

nodes.label: /model picker
nodes.rationale: The headless check and the picker read the same model list, so a model addressable in headless mode should appear in the picker.

nodes.label: PR #375
nodes.rationale: Built on a separate branch from main so the card branch is untouched; link check passed.

nodes.label: CommandCode custom provider
nodes.rationale: Added to existing settings using the COMMANDCODE_API_KEY already on the machine; the key is not printed or stored in the repository.

nodes.label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
nodes.rationale: Default Shipping model, chosen from a different company than the builder's; Claude models stay off the machine.

nodes.label: docs/agents/server-runbook.md
nodes.rationale: Added so nobody has to rediscover how to add a CommandCode model to Mastra Code; covers taking the exact id from CommandCode's list, adding it to the custom provider, using the mastracode/ prefix when the built-in list lacks the model, and proving it with a headless turn.

nodes.label: ~/.cache/mastra/provider-registry.json
nodes.rationale: Mastra Code's cached commandcode provider list (72 models) contains Kimi K3 and K2.7 but not K3.1 Pro, which is why the plain commandcode/ id returned Unknown model.

nodes.label: Mastra Code settings.json
nodes.rationale: Holds the CommandCode custom provider entry and the API key; a backup was made at settings.json.bak-kimi and the key was never printed or written into the repo.

nodes.label: apply-retry-fix.py
nodes.rationale: Fixes which retry policy matches a cut stream, not the missing deadline; the durable answer is a deadline per API call upstream plus the runner's own turn timeout.

nodes.label: scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr
nodes.rationale: Without env -u CLICOLOR_FORCE every GitHub status query fails with a JSON parse error and the watcher retries every 60s showing no statuses.

nodes.label: agent-instructions.js loading order
nodes.rationale: Loads global instruction files first, then one project file, preferring AGENTS.md over CLAUDE.md and stopping at the first file found.

nodes.label: ask_user tool
nodes.rationale: If the host removed it with disableBuiltinTools, ask in plain text.

nodes.label: push and pull_request CI twins
nodes.rationale: Separate concurrency groups, so cancel-in-progress does not dedupe them and both build at once; the pull_request run is the one the PR shows.

nodes.label: CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 in every shell
nodes.rationale: Makes gh colour --json output even into a pipe, so a JSON parser sees an escape byte; NO_COLOR=1 does not override it.

nodes.label: /bin/sh is dash
nodes.rationale: No PIPESTATUS, no process substitution, no arrays, so pipelines must be checked through a file and comparisons made against a saved copy.

nodes.label: DuckDB session traces
nodes.rationale: One DuckDB file per session because DuckDB admits one writer per file; a shared file leaves the second session's tracing off for its whole life.

nodes.label: Mastra Code hooks
nodes.rationale: Loaded from the session's project directory and from the user-level ~/.mastracode/hooks.json.

nodes.label: LibSQL store (mastra.db)
nodes.rationale: No per-session JSONL folder; threads and messages persist in mastra_threads and mastra_messages.

nodes.label: modelId override on subagent call
nodes.rationale: The call override wins over the controller's per-type model and the definition's defaultModelId; omitting modelId does not inherit the chat model.

nodes.label: task tools (task_write, task_update, task_complete, task_check)
nodes.rationale: The list persists in session state under tasks.

nodes.label: session thinkingLevel
nodes.rationale: Effort is session-scoped, not per subagent: there is no per-subagent effort field in the tool or in AgentControllerSubagent.

nodes.label: transient connection retry policy
nodes.rationale: Budget is MASTRACODE_TRANSIENT_CONNECTION_MAX_RETRIES = 10; emitTransientRetry is the only place carrying retryAttempt and maxRetries.

nodes.label: web job next/font/google flake
nodes.rationale: The push twin of a failing pull_request run passed on the same commit, so read the twin and run npm run build locally before treating the branch as broken.

nodes.label: ADR 0024
nodes.rationale: The stop ping hook was removed on 7 November 2026; the repository no longer wires a Notification hook.

nodes.label: root AGENTS.md
nodes.rationale: The root AGENTS.md wins over .mastracode/AGENTS.md, so the adapter and models file are named there; a .mastracode/AGENTS.md would never load while the root file exists.

nodes.label: arena skill
nodes.rationale: The cross-judge pool is a preference order, not a fan-out: one judge is tried from a family other than the parent chat's.

nodes.label: docs/plans/jul-276-start-screen.md
nodes.rationale: PR 6 of that plan carries the durable answer: a deadline per API call upstream plus the runner's own turn timeout.

nodes.label: ~/.agents/pstack-models.md
nodes.rationale: A plain file, not a rule the harness loads; the root AGENTS.md names it so sessions read it.

nodes.label: setup-pstack skill
nodes.rationale: Mastra Code has no plugin slash commands, so /setup-pstack is run by reading the skill file and following it.

nodes.label: Eval Blinding
nodes.rationale: No eval, test, judge, rubric, or benchmark terms in candidate-visible paths; the judge sees outputs by sanitized label only, never by model name.

nodes.label: Throughput Checkpoint
nodes.rationale: A dimension that genuinely does not apply keeps its item with n/a and a reason rather than being dropped, so the checkpoint stays complete.

nodes.label: Figure It Out Skill
nodes.rationale: When the task matches no playbook, the deliverable before any code is the workflow itself: phases that scale rigor to the task, run the scientific method, and leave a decision trail a human can audit after stepping away. Rigor is gates and artifacts, not 'try harder'.

nodes.label: Bug Fix Playbook
nodes.rationale: Every shipped line must trace to runtime evidence; belt-and-suspenders changes that might help are hypotheses, not fixes, and the smallest evidence-justified change ships.

nodes.label: Eval Playbook
nodes.rationale: Blinding prevents candidates from gaming the eval and keeps judge comparisons unbiased; chain-following is graded from transcripts and code shape, never self-report.

nodes.label: Feature Playbook
nodes.rationale: Code-coupled work goes to a single owner with the throughput checkpoint inline; parent-level fan-out is reserved for slices that produce independent artifacts.

nodes.label: $impeccable polish
nodes.rationale: polish reads the latest critique snapshot as its backlog and closes it when stale or cleared.

nodes.label: Adapt (web)
nodes.rationale: Adaptation is rethinking the experience for the new context, not scaling pixels; the trap is treating adaptation as scaling.

nodes.label: Adapt (native)
nodes.rationale: Restructure, don't stretch: a scaled-up phone UI on a tablet is the failure mode, so structure is driven from size classes rather than device-model checks.

nodes.label: Android platform reference
nodes.rationale: Material Design 3 governs structure, navigation, and interaction in every mode; brand expresses through Material's theming rather than off-spec components.

nodes.label: Animate
nodes.rationale: Motion must explain state, relationship, or hierarchy, or create one authored moment; decoration without purpose is animation debt.

nodes.label: Bolder
nodes.rationale: Bolder is an amplification request scoped to something that already exists; reaching for more effects is the opposite of bold.

nodes.label: Clarify
nodes.rationale: Interface text must say what happened, what matters, and what to do next while preserving factual meaning and brand voice.

nodes.label: Colorize
nodes.rationale: Color is introduced as hierarchy, meaning, and atmosphere; confirmed brand and semantic conventions are preserved rather than replaced.

nodes.label: Craft (deprecated alias)
nodes.rationale: craft is a deprecated alias for an ordinary request to make new visual work; it adds no setup, checkpoint, or quality behavior of its own.

nodes.label: Delight
nodes.rationale: Delight is product character revealed through a useful interaction, not a layer of generic whimsy; it must never delay or block the primary task.

nodes.label: Distill
nodes.rationale: Simplicity is not removing features but removing obstacles between users and their goals; every element must justify its existence.

nodes.label: Doctor
nodes.rationale: Maintenance, not design: it repairs schema drift mechanically and hands truth drift to the commands that own those documents.

nodes.label: Extract flow
nodes.rationale: Only extract things used 3+ times with the same intent; premature abstraction is worse than duplication.

nodes.label: Harden
nodes.rationale: Designs that only work with perfect data aren't production-ready, so the interface is hardened against real inputs, errors, languages, and network conditions.

nodes.label: Init flow (PRODUCT.md)
nodes.rationale: init captures durable product truth only; it does not invent a visual world or write DESIGN.md, which new-work and document own.

nodes.label: iOS platform reference
nodes.rationale: HIG conformance governs structure, navigation, and interaction in every mode; brand expresses through the layer the platform leaves open.

nodes.label: Layout
nodes.rationale: Layout turns product priority into reading order, grouping, rhythm, and usable space; the structural problem is diagnosed before moving boxes.

nodes.label: ops/julia-dashboard.service
nodes.rationale: Restart=always with RestartSec=2 and StartLimitIntervalSec=0 is what makes crash recovery work; without the zero start limit systemd stops restarting after five fast crashes.

nodes.label: mastracode resume
nodes.rationale: mastracode -t is a headless-only option needing --prompt; the interactive CLI silently starts a new chat, so the interactive command is mastracode resume <thread-id>.

nodes.label: One installed unit for every lane
nodes.norm_label: one installed unit for every lane
nodes.rationale: systemd unit names are global, so ten independent installs are not possible on one server; one unit reused per lane proves the same unit the server will run.

nodes.label: Stop ping
nodes.rationale: The --global entry exits without a ping when the session's own project already wires stop-ping.mjs, so one stop stays one comment and one reminder.

nodes.label: Thread-card binding
nodes.rationale: A chat with no card falls back to the card the last recorded stop belonged to and remembers it in thread-cards.json so later stops do not drift to another card.

nodes.label: Updater
nodes.rationale: The deploy checkout follows main and nothing else, so after a squash merge it must move onto the ref by itself rather than comparing ancestry.
